body.text: namo bhagavatyai āryamahāpratisarāyai |
body.translated_text: Homage to the Blessed Lady <s>Āryamahāpratisarā</s>!

children.translated_text: The supreme [treasury] for accomplishing the welfare of the world, adorned with many jewels,
the incomparable treasury of the True <s>Dharma</s> (teaching) — let the wise come to hear it!
Let the hosts of <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons), great <s>uragas</s> (serpents), and <s>daityas</s> (titans) come,
devoted to the rites of worship, along with <s>garuḍas</s> and kings of men! || 1 ||
This noble <s>Pratisarā</s>, protectress by mere remembrance,
skilled in the rites of protection for the entire world —
praised by those <s>Tathāgatas</s> (Buddhas) with hundreds of hymns,
the repository of the accomplishment of all aims — I bow down to her again and again. || 2 ||

children.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam | ekasmin samaye bhagavān mahāvajrameruśikharakūṭāgāre viharati sma | mahāvajrasamādhibhūmipratiṣṭhāne mahāvajrakalpavṛkṣasamalaṃkṛte mahāvajrapuṣkiriṇīratnapadmaprabhodbhāsite mahāvajravālikāsaṃstṛtabhūmibhāge | mahāvajrādhiṣṭhāne mahāvajramaṇḍalamātre | śakrasya devānām indrasya bhavane | mahāvajrasiṃhāsanakoṭīniyutaśatasahasravirājite dharmadeśanāprātihāryasarvabuddhādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhite sarvadharmasamatāpraveśe sarvajñatāniryāte |
children.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling in the great <s>Vajra</s>-<s>Meru</s> peak pavilion, at the site established on the ground of the great <s>vajra</s>-<s>samādhi</s> (diamond concentration), adorned with great <s>vajra</s> wish-fulfilling trees, illuminated by jewel-lotuses in the great <s>vajra</s> lotus-pond, on a ground strewn with great <s>vajra</s> sand, in the great <s>vajra</s>-consecrated place measuring the extent of the great <s>vajra</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> (sacred circle), in the palace of <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, resplendent with ten million hundred thousand <s>koṭīs</s> (millions) of great <s>vajra</s> lion-thrones, consecrated by the empowerment of all Buddhas with the miracle of <s>Dharma</s>-teaching, entering the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena), proceeding from omniscience.

children.text: caturaśītibhir bodhisattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraiḥ sarvair ekajātipratibaddhair avaivartikair anuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau mahāsthāmaprāptair mahāvajravimokṣasamādhibuddhakṣetravikurvaṇaprātihāryasaṃdarśakaiḥ | ekakṣaṇalavamuhūrtasarvasattvacittacaritānupraveśavicitramadhurodāragambhīradharmadeśanāpratibhānaprātihāryasamanvāgatair anekabuddhakṣetratathāgatamahāpūjāmeghārcanāvimokṣamukhadhāraṇīsamādhivaśitābhijñāveṇikabodhyaṅgamārgabhūmipāramitopāyakauśalyasaṃgrahavastumaitrīkaruṇāmuditopekṣābalaviviktaparyavadātacittasaṃtānaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Together with eighty-four <s>koṭī</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, all bound by a single birth [to enlightenment], irreversible from supreme perfect enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), having attained great power, displaying the miraculous transformations of Buddha-fields through the liberation-<s>samādhi</s> of the great <s>vajra</s>, endowed with the miraculous eloquence of <s>Dharma</s>-teaching — profound, sweet, noble, and wondrous — entering the conduct and thoughts of all sentient beings in a single instant, moment, and hour, [and endowed with] the <s>dhāraṇī</s> (mystic formula), <s>samādhi</s>, mastery, supernatural knowledge, special factors of enlightenment, path, stages, <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), skill in means, bases of attraction, loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, equanimity, and strength — with minds purified, secluded, and cleansed — from the liberation-gate of the worship-clouds of great offerings to <s>Tathāgatas</s> of many Buddha-fields.

children.text: tadyathā | vajragarbheṇa ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena | vajragātreṇa ca | vajramatinā ca | vajrahastena ca | vajrasaṃhatena ca | vajranārāyaṇena ca | vajravikurvitena ca | vajrakūṭena ca | vajrarāśinā ca | suvajreṇa ca | vajraketunā ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena | evampramukhaiś caturaśītibhir bodhisattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraiḥ |
children.translated_text: Namely: the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> (great being) <s>Vajragarbha</s>, and <s>Vajragātra</s>, and <s>Vajramati</s>, and <s>Vajrahasta</s>, and <s>Vajrasaṃhata</s>, and <s>Vajranārāyaṇa</s>, and <s>Vajravikurvita</s>, and <s>Vajrakūṭa</s>, and <s>Vajrarāśi</s>, and <s>Suvajra</s>, and the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Vajraketu</s> — headed by these, eighty-four <s>koṭī</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>bodhisattvas</s>.

children.text: sambahulaiś ca mahāśrāvakaiḥ sarvair arhadbhiḥ kṣīṇāsravair ucchinnabhavasaṃyojanaiḥ samyagājñāsuvimuktacittaiḥ suvimuktaprajñair acintyaṛddhibalaprātihāryavikurvaṇamahāsthāmaprāptair asaṅgajñānadarśibhiḥ sarvair vigatamalair nirdagdhasarvakleśavāsanābījaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Together with a great number of great <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers), all being <s>arhats</s> (worthy ones), with defilements exhausted, bonds of existence cut off, minds well-liberated through right knowledge, well-liberated in wisdom, having attained great power of inconceivable miraculous transformations through <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power), seers of unobstructed knowledge, all free from impurity, with the seeds and residual impressions of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) completely burned away.

children.text: yad utāyuṣmatā ca śāradvatīputreṇa | āyuṣmatā ca pūrṇena maitrāyaṇīputreṇa | āyuṣmatā ca kaphiṇena | āyuṣmatā ca subhūtinā | āyuṣmatā ca mahāmaudgalyāyanena | āyuṣmatā ca cundena | āyuṣmatā ca nandena | āyuṣmatā ca mahākāśyapena | āyuṣmatā coruvilvākāśyapena | evampramukhaiḥ sambahulaiś ca mahāśrāvakaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Namely: the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> (Śāriputra), and the venerable <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s>, and the venerable <s>Kaphiṇa</s>, and the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, and the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, and the venerable <s>Cunda</s>, and the venerable <s>Nanda</s>, and the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, and the venerable <s>Uruvilvākāśyapa</s> — headed by these, together with a great number of great <s>śrāvakas</s>.

children.text: maheśvaradevaputrapramukhaiś cāsaṃkhyeyair aparimāṇānabhilāpyānabhilāpyaiḥ śuddhāvāsakāyikair devaputraiḥ | brahmaṇā ca sahāpatinā | brahmakāyikadevaputrapramukhaiḥ | suyāmena ca devaputreṇa | suyāmakāyikadevaputraparivāreṇa | saṃtuṣitena ca | nirmāṇaratinā ca | paranirmitavaśavartinā ca | śakreṇa ca devānām indreṇa sarvadevaputraparivāreṇa |
children.translated_text: Headed by the divine son <s>Maheśvara</s>, with innumerable, immeasurable, inexpressible <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> (Pure Abode) divine sons; and <s>Brahmā Sahāmpati</s>, headed by the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> divine sons; and the divine son <s>Suyāma</s> with his <s>Suyāmakāyika</s> divine son retinue; and <s>Saṃtuṣita</s> (Tuṣita); and <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>; and <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>; and <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, with his entire divine son retinue.

children.text: vemacitriṇā cāsurendreṇa | balinā ca | prahlādena ca | rāhuṇā ca | vairocanena ca | evampramukhair aparimitāprameyāsaṃkhyeyair asurendraiḥ |
children.translated_text: And the <s>asura</s>-lord <s>Vemacitrin</s>, and <s>Balin</s>, and <s>Prahlāda</s>, and <s>Rāhu</s>, and <s>Virocana</s> — headed by these, with limitless, immeasurable, innumerable <s>asura</s>-lords.

children.text: sāgareṇa ca nāgarājena | takṣakena ca | vāsukinā ca | śaṅkhapālena ca | karkoṭakena ca | padmena ca | mahāpadmena ca | evampramukhair aparimitāprameyāsaṃkhyeyair nāgarājaiḥ |
children.translated_text: And the <s>nāga</s>-king <s>Sāgara</s>, and <s>Takṣaka</s>, and <s>Vāsuki</s>, and <s>Śaṅkhapāla</s>, and <s>Karkoṭaka</s>, and <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> — headed by these, with limitless, immeasurable, innumerable <s>nāga</s>-kings.

children.text: drumeṇa ca kiṃnararājena | anekakiṃnararājaparivāreṇa | pañcaśikhena ca gandharvarājena | anekagandharvarājaparivāreṇa | sarvārthasiddhena ca vidyādhararājena | anekavidyādhararājaparivāreṇa | suparṇākṣena ca garuḍarājena | anekagaruḍarājaparivāreṇa | vaiśravaṇena ca | māṇibhadreṇa ca | pūrṇabhadreṇa ca | pāñcikena ca mahāyakṣarājena | anekayakṣarājaparivāreṇa |
children.translated_text: And the <s>kiṃnara</s>-king <s>Druma</s> with a retinue of many <s>kiṃnara</s>-kings; and the <s>gandharva</s>-king <s>Pañcaśikha</s> with a retinue of many <s>gandharva</s>-kings; and the <s>vidyādhara</s>-king <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> with a retinue of many <s>vidyādhara</s>-kings; and the <s>garuḍa</s>-king <s>Suparṇākṣa</s> with a retinue of many <s>garuḍa</s>-kings; and <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, and <s>Māṇibhadra</s>, and <s>Pūrṇabhadra</s>, and the great <s>yakṣa</s>-king <s>Pāñcika</s> with a retinue of many <s>yakṣa</s>-kings.

children.text: hārītyā ca pañcaputraśataparivārayā | saptabhiś ca lokamātṛbhiḥ | saptabhiś ca mahārākṣasībhiḥ | saptabhiś ca maharṣibhiḥ | antarīkṣacaraiś ca | sarvanakṣatragrahadevataiḥ | digbhiś ca vidigbhiś ca | pṛthivyā ca sarasvatyā ca | bhūtaiś ca | vighnaiś ca | vināyakaiś ca | pretabhūtamahardhikaiḥ | sarvaiś ca parvatarājaiḥ | varuṇena ca lokapālena sarvasamudraparivāreṇa | virūḍhakena ca | virūpākṣeṇa ca | daṇḍapāṇinā ca | nairṛtena ca | jātavedasā ca | saptabhiś ca mahāvāyubhiḥ | īśānena ca sapatnīkena anekagaṇakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparivāreṇa | nārāyaṇena ca saparivāreṇa | dattakena ca | dāmakena ca | lohakena ca | mahāgaṇapatinā ca | megholkena ca | vināyakendreṇa | anekavighnavināyakaparivāreṇa | ṣaṣṭyā ca koṭarayā | catasṛbhiś ca bhaginībhiḥ sabhrātṛkābhiḥ | vajrasaṃkalayā ca | catuḥṣaṣṭibhiś ca vajradūtībhiḥ | vajrasenena ca | subāhunā ca | mūrdhaṭakena ca | anekavajrakulaparivāreṇa | tadanyaiś ca buddhadharmasaṃghābhiprasannair aparimitāprameyāsaṃkhyeyair devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakiṃnaramahoragabhūtapretapiśāconmādāpasmārasādhyamahallakaustārakaiḥ | sūryeṇa ca devaputreṇa | candreṇa ca devaputreṇa | saṃdhyayā ca devatayā | uṣayā ca devatayā | sarvaiś ca ṛtubhiḥ | rodasinyā ca sārdham |
children.translated_text: And <s>Hārītī</s> with her retinue of five hundred sons; and the seven world-mothers; and seven great <s>rākṣasīs</s> (demonesses); and seven great <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages); and those who move through the atmosphere; and all the deities of the <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions) and planets; and the cardinal and intermediate directions; and <s>Pṛthivī</s> (Earth) and <s>Sarasvatī</s>; and <s>bhūtas</s> (spirits); and <s>vighnas</s> (obstacle-makers); and <s>vināyakas</s> (removers of obstacles); and powerful ghosts and spirits; and all the mountain-kings; and <s>Varuṇa</s> the world-guardian with his retinue of all oceans; and <s>Virūḍhaka</s>; and <s>Virūpākṣa</s>; and <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s>; and <s>Nairṛta</s>; and <s>Jātavedas</s> (Fire); and the seven great winds; and <s>Īśāna</s> with his consort and a retinue of many <s>gaṇa</s>-<s>koṭī</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands; and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> with his retinue; and <s>Dattaka</s>; and <s>Dāmaka</s>; and <s>Lohaka</s>; and great <s>Gaṇapati</s>; and <s>Megholka</s>; and <s>Vināyakendra</s> with a retinue of many obstacle-<s>vināyakas</s>; and the sixty <s>Koṭarā</s>; and the four sisters with their brothers; and <s>Vajrasaṃkalā</s>; and the sixty-four <s>vajra</s>-messengers; and <s>Vajrasena</s>; and <s>Subāhu</s>; and <s>Mūrdhaṭaka</s>; with a retinue of many <s>vajra</s>-families; and others besides — limitless, immeasurable, innumerable <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kiṃnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, <s>bhūtas</s>, <s>pretas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, <s>unmādas</s> (madness spirits), <s>apasmāras</s> (epilepsy spirits), <s>sādhyas</s>, <s>mahallakas</s>, and <s>austārakas</s> — all devoted to the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>; and the divine son <s>Sūrya</s>; and the divine son <s>Candra</s>; and the deity <s>Saṃdhyā</s> (Twilight); and the deity <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn); and all the seasons; and together with <s>Rodasī</s> (Heaven-and-Earth).

children.text:
ity api bhagavān supravartitadharmacakraḥ supariniṣṭhitabuddhakāryaḥ suparipūrṇapuṇyajñānasaṃbhāraḥ suparigṛhītasarvajñatāmahābodhipāramitābhūmilābho jvalitadvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇālaṃkṛtaśarīraś caturaśītyanuvyañjanavirājitasarvāṅgāvayavaśobhaḥ sarvasattvānavalokitamūrdhānirjitaḥ sarvamārakarmakovidaḥ sarvasattvajñānapañcavidhacakṣuḥ sarvākāravaropetasarvajñajñānasamanvāgataḥ sarvabuddhadharmasamanvāgataḥ sarvamāraparapravādipramathana udgatakīrtiśabdaśloka ārṣabhasiṃhanādanādī samucchinnāvidyāndhakāro 'saṃkhyeyāparimāṇakalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasradānaśīlakṣāntivīryadhyānaprajñopāyabalapraṇidhānajñānapāramitāprāpto duṣkaracaryāvinivartito dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇacaturaśītyanuvyañjanālaṃkṛtagātraśobhaḥ mahāvajraratnapadmagarbhasiṃhāsane anekavajraratnamuktākiṅkiṇījālakalakalonnādite anekavajraratnavedikāpādapīṭhasupratiṣṭhite anekavajraratnamakaramukhodgīrṇalohitamuktāvalīnibaddhagaṇḍūṣake anekavajraratnapadmakarṇikāvilagnakarketanendranīlamahānīlapuṣparāgaraśmijvālāvabhāsite samantaprāsādike anekavajraratnaśalākāvibhūṣitoddaṇḍātapatrakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrakṛtachāyāparikare anekakalpadrumopaśobhitavistāre sumerumātre vajraratnapadmāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ |
kāñcanaparvatarāja iva śriyā jvalan sūryasahasrātirekaprabhāmaṇḍalavirājitabhūmibhāgaḥ suparipūrṇacandra iva sarvalokapriyadarśano mahākalpavṛkṣa iva buddhadharmasaṃkusumito dharmaṃ deśayati sma ādau kalyāṇaṃ madhye kalyāṇaṃ paryavasāne kalyāṇaṃ svarthaṃ suvyañjanaṃ kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ saṃprakāśayati sma |
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), who had well turned the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, who had well accomplished the Buddha's work, who had well fulfilled the accumulation of merit and knowledge, who had attained the great <s>Bodhi</s>-perfection of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) at all stages, whose body was adorned with the blazing thirty-two marks of a <s>Mahāpuruṣa</s> (Great Being), whose entire body and limbs shone with eighty minor marks, who towered above all beings with his unsurpassed crown, who was skilled in all the works of <s>Māra</s>, who possessed the five kinds of eyes of knowledge of all beings, who was endowed with omniscient knowledge possessing all aspects and excellences, who was endowed with all the qualities of a Buddha, who crushed all <s>Māras</s> and opposing doctrines, whose fame, renown, and glory had risen, who roared the lion's roar of the <s>Ṛṣabha</s> (bull), who had extinguished the darkness of ignorance, who had attained the perfections of giving, morality, patience, vigor, meditation, wisdom, skillful means, power, aspiration, and knowledge through innumerable, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), who had completed the practice of austerities, whose body shone adorned with the thirty-two marks of a <s>Mahāpuruṣa</s> and eighty minor marks—was seated on a great <s>vajra</s>-jewel-lotus-womb lion-throne, resounding with the tinkling of many <s>vajra</s>-jewel-pearl nets of bells, well-established on many <s>vajra</s>-jewel platforms and footstools, bound with garlands of red pearls poured forth from many <s>vajra</s>-jewel <s>makara</s> (sea-creature) mouths, illuminated by the radiant flames of <s>indranīla</s>, <s>mahānīla</s>, and <s>puṣparāga</s> gems attached to <s>vajra</s>-jewel lotus calyxes, surrounded on all sides, adorned with hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of raised parasols decorated with <s>vajra</s>-jewel rods providing shade, of vast extent beautified by many wish-fulfilling trees, on a <s>vajra</s>-jewel-lotus seat as great as Mount <s>Sumeru</s>. Blazing with splendor like the golden king of mountains, with the surface of the earth illuminated by a halo of radiance surpassing a thousand suns, lovely to behold by all the world like a perfectly full moon, blossoming with the flowers of <s>Buddhadharma</s> like a great wish-fulfilling tree—he was teaching the <s>Dharma</s>: beautiful in the beginning, beautiful in the middle, beautiful in the end; proclaiming the holy life that is good in meaning, good in expression, complete, perfect, pure, and stainless.

children.text: atha khalu bhagavān mūrdhnaḥ saṃdher ūrṇākośāt sarvabuddhasaṃdarśanaṃ nāma raśmijālaṃ pramuñcati sma | tena ca raśmijālenāyaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātur avabhāsitaḥ sphuṭīkṛto 'bhūt | yāvanti ca gaṅgānadīvālikopamāni buddhakṣetrāṇi tāni sarvāṇi tenāvabhāsena sphuṭāny abhūvan | ye ca teṣu buddhakṣetreṣu buddhā bhagavanto 'nekasiṃhāsanavyūhakūṭāgāravimāneṣu dharmaṃ deśayanti sma sārdhaṃ mahāśrāvakair bodhisattvair mahāsattvair bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikābhir devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakiṃnaramahoragaiḥ | atha khalu bhagavān vistīrṇāṃ parṣadam āmantrayate sma |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> released from the juncture of his crown and the <s>ūrṇā</s>-tuft a net of rays called 'Vision of All Buddhas.' By that net of rays this great trichiliocosm was illuminated and made manifest. And as many buddha-fields as there are—equal to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>—all of them became manifest by that illumination. And the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in those buddha-fields were teaching the <s>Dharma</s> in many lion-throne-arrayed pavilion-palaces, together with great <s>Śrāvakas</s> (disciples), <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and <s>Mahāsattvas</s>, monks and nuns, laymen and laywomen, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kiṃnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the vast assembly:
"I shall proclaim <s>Pratisarā</s> out of compassion for all beings;
this <s>dhāraṇī</s> (protective spell) destroys all evil deeds, the crusher of all malevolent ones. (1)
By merely hearing her, sins are utterly destroyed;
she bestows happiness on all beings and liberates from all diseases. (2)
Out of compassion for all beings, she was spoken by the Lord of the World;
for the protection of all embodied beings who are headed to unfortunate rebirths. (3)
One who has been protected by her may enter the abode of the <s>Asuras</s>,

children.text: aḍakavatīṃ tathā gacched rākṣasāṇām ālayaṃ bhuvi || 4 ||
children.translated_text: may go to <s>Aḍakavatī</s> and to the dwelling of <s>Rākṣasas</s> on earth. (4)
In a terrible and fierce battle with <s>Bhūtas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, and <s>Piśācas</s>,
one becomes unassailable by all enemies and by all hosts of beings. (5)
All planetary afflictions (<s>grahas</s>) are destroyed by the recitation and invocation of the name;
<s>Skanda</s>-seizures, madness, epilepsy, <s>Piśācas</s>, and <s>Ḍākinīs</s> likewise. (6)
The vitality-devourers of great power who harm human beings—

children.text: te sarve stambhitā bhonti pratisarasyaiva tejasā || 7 ||
children.translated_text: they are all paralyzed by the power of <s>Pratisarā</s> alone. (7)

children.text: paracakrā vinaśyanti kākhordā ye ca dāruṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: Hostile armies are destroyed, and the terrible <s>Kākhordas</s> (sorcerers);

children.text: mantrakarmā na bādhante mūlakarmāc ca mucyate || 8 ||
children.translated_text: spell-workings do not afflict, and one is freed from root-sorcery. (8)

children.text: na viṣaṃ na garaṃ nāgni na śastraṃ naiva codakam |
children.translated_text: Neither poison, nor noxious substance, nor fire, nor weapon, nor water,

children.text: aśanir vidyutaś caiva kālavāyur na bādhate || 9 ||
children.translated_text: neither thunderbolt nor lightning, nor the wind of death can harm [the bearer]. (9)
One crushes all enemies by the power of this <s>Vidyārājñī</s> (Queen of Spells);

children.text: sarve 'rthās tasya sidhyanti jayaṃ prāpnoti nityaśaḥ || 10 ||
children.translated_text: all aims are accomplished for that person, and victory is attained perpetually. (10)

children.text: yaḥ kaścid dhārayed vidyāṃ kaṇṭhe bāhau baddhāpi vā |
children.translated_text: Whoever bears this <s>vidyā</s> (spell) on the neck or bound on the arm,

children.text: tasya sarvāṇi kāryāṇi sidhyante nātra saṃśayaḥ || 11 ||
children.translated_text: all their undertakings are accomplished—there is no doubt in this. (11)

children.text: nityaṃ rakṣanti devendrā nāgarājās tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: The lords of the <s>Devas</s> constantly protect [the bearer], and the <s>Nāga</s>-kings likewise,
<s>Bodhisattvas</s> of great valor, Buddhas, and <s>Pratyeka</s>-leaders, (12)
the <s>Śrāvakas</s> of all Buddhas, the <s>Vidyā</s>-goddesses of great supernatural power—
they constantly provide protection to the bearer of <s>Pratisarā</s>. (13)

children.text: vajrapāṇiś ca yakṣendro rājānaś caturas tathā |
children.translated_text: <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, lord of the <s>Yakṣas</s>, and the four kings likewise—

children.text: tasya rakṣāṃ kariṣyanti divārātrau na saṃśayaḥ || 14 ||
children.translated_text: they will provide protection day and night, without doubt. (14)
<s>Śakra</s> together with the thirty [gods], <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>,
<s>Nandikeśa</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>, <s>Kārttikeya</s>, and <s>Gaṇeśvara</s>— (15)
all the hosts of <s>Mātṛs</s> (Mothers), and others belonging to <s>Māra</s>'s retinue,

children.text: ṛṣayaś ca mahātejā devāś caiva maharddhikāḥ || 16 ||
children.translated_text: the great seers of mighty power, and the gods of great supernatural ability— (16)
they will constantly provide protection to the bearer of <s>Pratisarā</s>.
And the Buddhas, great souls, and the <s>Vidyā</s>-goddesses of great strength: (17)
<s>Māmakī</s>, <s>Bhṛkuṭī</s>, goddess <s>Tārā</s>, and <s>Aṅkuśī</s>,
<s>Vajrasaṃkalā</s>, <s>Śvetā</s>, and <s>Mahāśvetā</s> likewise, (18)

children.text: mahākālī ca dūtyaś ca vajradūtyas tathā parāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Mahākālī</s>, the messengers, the <s>Vajra</s>-messengers and other supreme ones,
<s>Supāśī</s>, <s>Vajrapāśī</s>, <s>Vajrapāṇī</s> of great strength, (19)
<s>Vajramālā</s>, the great <s>Vidyā</s>, and likewise <s>Amṛtakuṇḍalī</s>,
<s>Aparājitā</s>, the great goddess, <s>Kālakarṇī</s> of great power, (20)

children.text: tathā dhanyā mahābhāgā padmakuṇḍalir eva ca |
children.translated_text: likewise <s>Dhanyā</s> of great fortune, and <s>Padmakuṇḍalī</s> too,
<s>Puṣpadantī</s>, <s>Maṇicūḍā</s>, <s>Svarṇakeśī</s>, and <s>Piṅgalā</s>, (21)

children.text: mahātejā tathā devī dhanyā ca vidyunmālinī |
children.translated_text: the great-powered goddess <s>Dhanyā</s> and <s>Vidyunmālinī</s>,
the <s>Rākṣasī</s> <s>Ekajaṭā</s>, and the Buddha [goddesses], rulers of the earth, (22)
<s>Kāpālinī</s> of great fortune, <s>Dhanyā</s>, and <s>Laṅkeśvarī</s> likewise,
and many other <s>vidyās</s> (spells) that benefit all beings— (23)

children.text: tasya rakṣāṃ kariṣyanti yasya vidyā kare sthitā |
children.translated_text: they will provide protection to the one in whose hand this <s>vidyā</s> abides.
<s>Hārītī</s> and <s>Pāñcika</s>, <s>Śaṅkhinī</s>, and <s>Kūṭadantinī</s>— (24)

children.text: śrīdevī sarasvatī caiva taṃ rakṣanti sadānugāḥ |
children.translated_text: goddess <s>Śrī</s> and <s>Sarasvatī</s> protect that one, always following [the bearer].

children.text: mahāpratisarām etāṃ yā strī dhārayate sadā || 25 ||
children.translated_text: A woman who always bears this <s>Mahāpratisarā</s>, (25)

children.text: sarvasiddhir bhavet tasyāḥ putragarbhā ca nityaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: all accomplishments shall be hers, and she shall always carry a son in her womb.

children.text: sukhaṃ garbhāṇi vardhante sukhaṃ prasūyati gurviṇī || 26 ||
children.translated_text: The wombs grow happily, and the pregnant woman gives birth with ease. (26)

children.text: vyādhayaś cāpi naśyanti sarvapāpā na saṃśayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Diseases are destroyed and all sins—there is no doubt.
Ever meritorious and strong, one increases in wealth and grain. (27)
One whose words are heeded and who shall be worthy of worship—

children.text: śucir dhārayate yas tu striyo vā puruṣo 'pi vā || 28 ||
children.translated_text: whoever bears [this <s>dhāraṇī</s>] in purity, whether woman or man, (28)
that one shall be devoted to the liberation of all beings,
and shall always be happy, free from all diseases. (29)
Kings become subject to that person, together with the inner palace and great retinue;

children.text: nityaṃ ca jvalate lakṣmyā puṇyarāśir vivardhate || 30 ||
children.translated_text: one always blazes with prosperity, and the heap of merit increases. (30)
All ritual practices are accomplished, having entered every <s>maṇḍala</s>;
that one is a knower of all <s>samayas</s> (pledges), just as [stated in] the word of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor). (31)
Bad dreams do not afflict; it is the supreme remover of all sins;

children.text: kilbiṣāś caiva naśyanti pratyamitrās tathaiva ca || 32 ||
children.translated_text: offenses are destroyed, and adversaries likewise. (32)
It was spoken by the great lords of knowledge for the destruction of all planetary afflictions;

children.text: sarvakāmaṃdadā hy eṣā bhāvayed yas tu nityaśaḥ || 33 ||
children.translated_text: this [<s>dhāraṇī</s>] fulfills all desires—one who practices it constantly [attains all]. (33)

body.text: tad idānīṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi bhūtasaṃghāḥ śṛṇotha me |
body.translated_text: Now I shall proclaim it—listen to me, O hosts of beings!"

children.translated_text: <s>Namaḥ</s> to all <s>Tathāgatas</s>! <s>Namo namaḥ</s> to the <s>Saṃgha</s> of all Buddhas and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>!

body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s> O you of vast womb! O vastly pure one! O you of victorious womb! O you of <s>vajra</s>-flame womb! O you deep in paths! O purifier of the sky! O purifier of all sins! <s>Oṃ</s> O virtuous one! O sky-wanderer! <s>gagariṇi</s>, <s>giri giri</s>, <s>gamari gamari</s>, <s>gaha gaha</s>, <s>gargāri gargāri</s>, <s>gagari gagari</s>, <s>gambhari gambhari</s>, <s>gabhi gabhi</s>, <s>gahi gahi</s>, <s>gamani</s>, <s>gare</s>, <s>guha guha</s>, <s>guhani guhani</s>, <s>cale</s>, <s>mucile</s>, O victorious one! O you who bring victory! O you freed from all fears! O you who gather the womb! <s>siri siri</s>, <s>miri miri</s>, <s>ghiri ghiri</s>! O you who attract from all directions! O you who crush all enemies! Protect, protect me and all beings! <s>ciri ciri</s>! O you free from obstructions! O destroyer of obstructions! <s>suri suri</s>, <s>muri muri</s>, <s>cili cili</s>! O lotus! O pure one! O victorious one! O you who bring victory! O victorious one! O blessed one! O wearer of a jewel-crown garland! O you who bear many varied and wonderful garments! O blessed one! O great <s>Vidyā</s>-goddess! Protect, protect me and all beings everywhere in all directions! O purifier of all sins! <s>huru huru</s>! Protect, protect me and all beings, the helpless, the unprotected, the shelterless! Free me from all sufferings! O fierce one, fierce one! O fierce woman! O swift one! O you who ward off all the wicked! O you who carry victory! <s>huru huru</s>, <s>muru muru</s>, <s>curu curu</s>! O protector of life! O you who crush the best of demons! O you worshipped by all hosts of gods! <s>dhiri dhiri</s>! O you who survey all directions! O radiant one, radiant one! O you of pure radiance! O purifier of all sins! Hold, hold! O earth-bearer! <s>sumu sumu</s>! <s>musu musu</s>! <s>ruru cale</s>! Set the wicked in motion! Fulfill our hopes! O you who bear a glorious form! O victorious lotus! <s>kṣiṇi kṣiṇi</s>! O you with the goad of boons! <s>Oṃ</s> O you purified by the lotus! Purify, purify! O pure one! <s>bhara bhara</s>, <s>bhiri bhiri</s>, <s>bhuru bhuru</s>! O you purified by auspiciousness! O you of holy face! O sword-bearer, sword-bearer! <s>khara khara</s>! O blazing peak! O you whose purity shines forth spread in all directions! Blaze, blaze! O you who attract all hosts of gods! O you of truthful vows! Cross, cross! Carry across, carry across me and all beings! O you gazed upon by <s>Nāgas</s>! <s>lahu lahu</s>, <s>hulu hulu</s>, <s>hutu hutu</s>, <s>turu turu</s>, <s>kiṇi kiṇi</s>, <s>kṣiṇi kṣiṇi</s>! O you who devour all planetary afflictions! <s>piṅgali piṅgali</s>! <s>mucu mucu</s>, <s>cumu cumu</s>, <s>sumu sumu</s>! O you of excellent discernment! Cross, cross! O you gazed upon by <s>Nāgas</s>! Carry across me and all beings, O blessed one, from the eight great fears, everywhere with a complete binding of the directions, with a <s>vajra</s>-wall and <s>vajra</s>-noose binding! O you purified by <s>vajra</s>-flame! <s>bhuri bhuri</s>! O blessed one! O you who bear the womb! O purifier of the womb! O you who fill the belly! Blaze, blaze! Move, move! O flaming one! May the god rain divine water everywhere! O you who shower nectar! O you who cause the descent of deities! Consecrate me and all beings! To you of the form of the excellent nectar of the words of the best of <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones)! Protect, protect me and all beings everywhere, at all times, from all fears, from all calamities, from all misfortunes, from all diseases, from all fearful terrors of the wicked! O purifier of all quarrels, disputes, conflicts, contentions, bad dreams, ill omens, inauspiciousness, and sin! O you who tear apart all <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and <s>Nāgas</s>! Strong, strong! O powerful one! Conquer, conquer! May I be victorious everywhere at all times! May this great <s>Vidyā</s> (spell) succeed for me! Accomplish the <s>maṇḍala</s>! Destroy the obstacles! Conquer, conquer! O perfected one! Succeed, succeed! Awaken, awaken! Fulfill, fulfill! O fulfiller, fulfiller! Fulfill our hopes! O you whose form has arisen from all <s>Vidyās</s>! O supreme victorious one! O victorious one! Stand firm, stand firm! Guard the vow! O you purified by the heart of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>! Look upon me and all beings in the eight great terrible fears! Move, move! Advance, advance! O purifier of all obstructions! O you purified in the <s>maṇḍala</s> of all forms! O you freed, freed! O you free from stain! O purifier! <s>kṣiṇi kṣiṇi</s>! O you purified of all sin! O you free from defilement! O you of radiant power! O you of <s>vajra</s>-power! To those consecrated by all deities, <s>svāhā</s>! To the heart empowered by the hearts of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the fulfillment of the vow of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!
