body.text: samantajvālāmālāviśuddhisphuritacintāmaṇimudrāhṛdayāparājitā dhāraṇī asyā mahāpratisarāmahāvidyārājñyāḥ |
body.translated_text: [This is] the <s>Samantajvālāmālāviśuddhisphuritacintāmaṇimudrāhṛdaya</s> invincible <s>dhāraṇī</s> (The Dhāraṇī of the Heart-Seal of the Wish-Fulfilling Gem Blazing with the Pure Garland of All-Pervading Flames) of this <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s> (Great Protectress, Great Queen of Spells).

children.text: sahaśravaṇamātreṇāyaṃ mahābrāhmaṇa tasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhitur vā sarvapāpavinirmuktir bhavati | yasya punar iyaṃ hṛdayagatā bhavati sa mahābrāhmaṇa vajrakāya iti veditavyaḥ | nāgnis tasya kāye kramiṣyati | kim iti saṃjñātam |
children.translated_text: By the mere hearing of it, O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, that son of good family or daughter of good family becomes freed from all sins. Moreover, he in whose heart this [<s>vidyā</s>] dwells — that one, O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, should be known as having a <s>vajra</s>-body (diamond body). Fire will not approach his body. How is this known?

children.text: yadā kapilavastuni mahānagaravare rāhulabhadraḥ kumāro mātuḥ kukṣigato 'bhūt tadā gopayā śākyakanyayā ātmānam agnikhadāyāṃ prakṣiptaḥ | tatra padminī prādurbhūtā | tadā rāhulabhadraḥ kumāraḥ kukṣigata imāṃ vidyāṃ manasy akārṣīt | asyā vidyāyā anusmaraṇamātreṇa so 'gnis tasmin kṣaṇe śītībhāvam upagataḥ | tato gopāyāḥ śākyakanyāyāḥ śarīram agninā na spṛṣṭam iti |
children.translated_text: When in <s>Kapilavastu</s>, the great and excellent city, the prince <s>Rāhulabhadra</s> was in the womb of his mother, then <s>Gopā</s>, the <s>Śākya</s> princess, threw herself into a fire-pit. There a lotus appeared. Then the prince <s>Rāhulabhadra</s>, while still in the womb, brought this <s>vidyā</s> (sacred knowledge) to mind. By the mere recollection of this <s>vidyā</s>, that fire in that very instant became cool. Thus the body of <s>Gopā</s>, the <s>Śākya</s> princess, was not touched by fire.

children.text: tat kasya hetoḥ | eṣā vidyā sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhitā | tena hetunā mahābrāhmaṇāgnir na dahati | na ca viṣeṇa śakyaṃ jīvitād vyaparopayitum | tat katham iti |
children.translated_text: For what reason? This <s>vidyā</s> is empowered by the consecration of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> (Buddhas). For that reason, O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, fire does not burn [the bearer], nor can one be deprived of life by poison. How is this so?

children.text: yadā mahābrāhmaṇa śūrpārake mahānagaravare kośabalikasya śreṣṭhinaḥ putro vidyāvādiko babhūva tena tadvidyābalena takṣako nāgarājā ākarṣitaḥ | ākarṣayitvā ca pramādavaśād baddho na dāntaḥ | yāvat tenāsau krodhād daṣṭaḥ sa tīvrāṃ vedanāṃ vedayati | jānāti ca yathā me jīvitaṃ niruddham iti | tatra bahavo vādikā āhūtā na ca kaścic chaknoti viṣaṃ ceṣṭayitum | atha tatraiva śūrpārake mahānagare vimalaśuddhir nāmopāsikā prativasati mahākaruṇāsamanvāgatā | tasyā iyaṃ mahāvidyārājñī mukhāgre 'bhūt | sā tasyāntikam upasaṃkrāntā upasaṃkramyemāṃ mahāvidyāṃ pravartayām āsa | ekavelāyām anusmṛtamātreṇa nirviṣaṃ smṛtiṃ pratilabdhaṃ kṛtvā tato mahāvyasanāt parimocayitvā imām eva mahāvidyāṃ hṛdayagatāṃ kārayati sma yathā vidhivad anujñātam iti |
children.translated_text: When, O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, in <s>Śūrpāraka</s>, the great and excellent city, the son of the merchant <s>Kośabalika</s> became a <s>vidyā</s>-practitioner (spell-caster), he summoned the <s>nāga</s>-king <s>Takṣaka</s> by the power of that <s>vidyā</s>. But having summoned him, through carelessness he bound him without taming him. Then, in anger, [the <s>nāga</s>] bit him, and he experienced intense pain. And he knew: "My life is coming to an end." Many spell-casters were summoned there, but none was able to counteract the poison. Now in that very city of <s>Śūrpāraka</s> there dwelt a lay-woman named <s>Vimalaśuddhi</s>, endowed with great compassion. This <s>Mahāvidyārājñī</s> (Great Queen of Sacred Knowledge) was on her lips. She approached him and set this great <s>vidyā</s> in motion. By mere recollection at a single occasion, the poison was neutralized, mindfulness was regained, and having liberated him from that great calamity, she caused this very great <s>vidyā</s> to dwell in his heart, as properly authorized.

children.text: api ca mahābrāhmaṇa kiṃ parijñātam iti |
children.translated_text: Moreover, O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, how is this known?

body.text: vārāṇasyāṃ mahānagaryām anupūrveṇānuvicaramāṇo rājā brahmadatta iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati | tasya prātisīmiko balacakrarājā caturaṅgaṃ balakāyaṃ saṃnāhya vārāṇasīṃ mahānagarīṃ parivārya vināśayitum ārabdhaḥ | tato rājño brahmadattasyāmātyair niveditam | deva paracakreṇa nagaram apahṛtam | kiṃ nu khalu vayam upāyaṃ kuryāmo yenaitat paracakraṃ vinaśyet | ājñāṃ prayaccha | rājā kathayati | alpotsukā bhavanto bhavatha | asti mama mahāpratisarā nāma mahāvidyārājñī yenāham imaṃ caturaṅgaṃ balakāyaṃ parājayiṣyāmi bhasmīkariṣyāmi ca | amātyāḥ śirasā praṇipatyocuḥ | kim idaṃ mahārāja | nāsmābhiḥ kadācid api śrutam iti | rājā prāha | aham idānīṃ pratyakṣadarśanaṃ kariṣyāmi | atha sa rājā brahmadatto nānāgandhodakena snātaśiraḥ śucivastraṃ prāvṛtya imaṃ mahāvidyārājaṃ yathāvidhinālikhya śiraḥkośe sthāpya imām eva vidyārājñīkavacaṃ kṛtvā saṃgrāmamadhye 'vatīrya ekākinaiva sarvo 'sau caturaṅgabalakāyaḥ parājitaḥ | āmardya ca tāvad anayā śaraṇaṃ gata iti kṛtvāsau balacakrarājā mukta
body.translated_text: In <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, the great city, wandering about in due course, there was a king known as <s>Brahmadatta</s>. His neighboring enemy king, having equipped a fourfold army, besieged the great city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> and began to destroy it. Then the ministers reported to King <s>Brahmadatta</s>: "Lord, the city has been seized by the enemy army. What strategy shall we employ so that this enemy force may be destroyed? Give the command." The king said: "Be of little concern, gentlemen. I have the <s>Mahāpratisarā</s> named <s>Mahāvidyārājñī</s> (Great Queen of Sacred Knowledge), by which I shall defeat and reduce to ashes this fourfold army." The ministers, bowing their heads, said: "What is this, O great king? We have never heard of such a thing." The king said: "I shall now give a direct demonstration." Then King <s>Brahmadatta</s>, having bathed his head with various fragrant waters and wrapped himself in clean garments, wrote this great <s>Vidyārāja</s> (King of Sacred Knowledge) according to the proper rite, placed it in a head-casket, made this very <s>Vidyārājñī</s> (Queen of Sacred Knowledge) into an armor, descended alone into the midst of battle, and that entire fourfold army was defeated. And having crushed them thoroughly, the enemy king, saying "I take refuge," was released.

children.text: iti mahābrāhmaṇa pratyakṣamahānubhāveyaṃ mahāvidyārājñī sarvatathāgatahṛdayamudrādhiṣṭhitā pratyakṣa eveti dhārayitavyā | sarvatathāgatasamaiṣā draṣṭavyā | paścime kāle paścime samaye alpāyuṣkāṇāṃ mandapuṇyānāṃ parīttabhāgyānāṃ sattvānāṃ hitāya draṣṭavyā | yaḥ kaścin mahābrāhmaṇa imāṃ mahāpratisarāṃ mahāvidyārājñīṃ yathāvidhinā likhitvā bāhau kaṇṭhe vā dhārayiṣyati sa sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhito veditavyaḥ | sarvatathāgatakāya iti veditavyaḥ | vajrakāya iti veditavyaḥ | sarvatathāgatadhātugarbha iti veditavyaḥ | sarvatathāgatanetra iti veditavyaḥ | jvalitārciḥśarīra iti veditavyaḥ | abhedyakavaca iti veditavyaḥ | sarvaśatrūṇāṃ pramathana iti veditavyaḥ | sarvapāpāvaraṇanirdahana iti veditavyaḥ | narakagativiśodhaka iti veditavyaḥ | kim iti pūrvaparijñātaṃ mahābrāhmaṇa |
children.translated_text: Thus, O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, this <s>Mahāvidyārājñī</s> is of directly manifest great power, empowered by the heart-seal of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, and should be upheld as directly efficacious. She should be regarded as equal to all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. In the last age, in the last period, she should be regarded as being for the benefit of beings of short lifespan, of little merit, and of scanty fortune. Whoever, O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having written this <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s> according to the proper rite, wears it on the arm or neck — he should be known as empowered by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; he should be known as the body of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; he should be known as having a <s>vajra</s>-body; he should be known as a receptacle of the relics of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; he should be known as the eye of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>; he should be known as one whose body blazes with radiance; he should be known as having impenetrable armor; he should be known as the crusher of all enemies; he should be known as the burner of all sin-obscurations; he should be known as the purifier of the realm of hell. How is this previously known, O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>?

children.text: anyatamasmin pradeśe bhikṣur aśrāddhas tathāgatakulaśikṣākhaṇḍakaḥ adattādāyī | sukhāyadvārahārikaḥ sāṃghikaṃ cāturdiśikaṃ gaṇaprāptaṃ ca yad dravyaṃ tat paudgalikaṃ sarvam adhiṣṭhāya bhakṣayati | yāvad apareṇa samayena mahatā vyādhinā spṛṣṭaḥ mahatīṃ duḥkhāṃ vedanām anubhavati | sa tapasvī atrāṇo 'pratisaraṇo mahāntam utkrośanaśabdaṃ karoti | atha tasminn eva pradeśe upāsako brāhmaṇaḥ prativasati | tena tacchabdaṃ śrutam | śrutvā ca punar yena sa bhikṣus tenopasaṃkrānta upasaṃkramya tasya bhikṣor imāṃ mahāpratisarāṃ mahāvidyārājñīṃ likhitvā kaṇṭhe badhnāti sma | samanantarabaddhe ca mahāpratisare tasya bhikṣoḥ sarvā vedanāḥ praśāntāḥ sarvavyādhibhiḥ parimuktaḥ svasthaḥ saṃvṛtta iti | sa tasyā eva rātryā atyayāt sūpasthitasmṛtiḥ kālagataḥ | sa tasmin kaḍevare utsṛṣṭe 'vīcau mahānarake upapannaḥ | tac ca tasya mṛtaśarīraṃ bhikṣubhiḥ kūṭe sthāpitam | sā tasya mahāpratisarā mahāvidyārājñī kaṇṭhe baddhaivāvasthitā | samanantaropapannasya tasya bhikṣos tasminn avīcau teṣāṃ nārakāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvaduḥkhavedanāḥ praśāntāḥ | te ca nārakāḥ sattvāḥ sarvasukhasamarpitā abhūvan | ye ca te mahāntā āvīcikā agniskandhās te 'pi sarveṇa sarvam upaśāntā iti | atha te yamapuruṣā vispandamānā yamasya dharmarājasyemaṃ niścayaṃ vistareṇārocayanti sma |
children.translated_text: In a certain region, a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) who was faithless, who violated the training rules of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s lineage, who took what was not given, who carried away [goods] through doors of convenience — whatever property belonged to the <s>Saṃgha</s> (monastic community), to the community of the four directions, or to the group, all that he appropriated as personal and consumed. In time, he was struck by a great illness and experienced intense painful sensations. The wretched one, without protection, without refuge, cried out with a great shrieking sound. Now in that very region there dwelt a lay-devotee, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. He heard that sound. Having heard it, he approached that <s>bhikṣu</s>, and having written this <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s>, he tied it around his neck. Immediately upon the <s>Mahāpratisarā</s> being bound, all the painful sensations of that <s>bhikṣu</s> were pacified; he was freed from all illnesses and became well. But that very night, with mindfulness well-established, he died. When that corpse was abandoned, he was reborn in <s>Avīci</s>, the great hell. That dead body of his was placed on a funeral pyre by the <s>bhikṣus</s>. The <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s> remained tied around his neck. Immediately upon that <s>bhikṣu</s>'s rebirth in that <s>Avīci</s> [hell], all the painful sensations of those hell-beings were pacified. And those hell-beings were endowed with all happiness. And those great fires of <s>Avīci</s> were completely and entirely extinguished. Then those servants of <s>Yama</s> (the Lord of Death), trembling, reported this matter in detail to <s>Yama</s>, the <s>Dharmarāja</s> (King of Righteousness):
"O Lord, a most astonishing thing is seen in the confines of hell:

children.text: praśāntā dāruṇā duḥkhāḥ sattvānāṃ karmajāś ca ye || 1 ||
children.translated_text: the terrible sufferings born of <s>karma</s> (actions) of beings have been pacified. || 1 ||

children.text: praśāntās te 'pi aṅgārā dehasthā dehināṃ sadā |
children.translated_text: Even the embers dwelling in the bodies of embodied beings are forever pacified;

children.text: karapattrā na bādhante kṣuradhārā na sajjate || 2 ||
children.translated_text: the saws do not torment, the razor-edges do not cut. || 2 ||

children.text: astrāś ca bhagnāḥ sarve praśāntā lohakumbhayaḥ |
children.translated_text: All the weapons are broken, the iron cauldrons are pacified;

children.text: asipattravane pattrā na bādhante karmajāḥ punaḥ || 3 ||
children.translated_text: in the <s>Asipattravana</s> (Sword-leaf Forest), the karma-born leaves no longer torment. || 3 ||

children.text: yamas tvaṃ dharmarājo 'si dharmeṇa śāsayase nṛṇām |
children.translated_text: You, O <s>Yama</s>, are the <s>Dharmarāja</s> (King of Righteousness); you govern humans by <s>dharma</s> (law);

children.text: idaṃ tu kāraṇaṃ nālpaṃ tvam asmākaṃ vaktum arhasi || 4 ||
children.translated_text: this is no small matter — you should explain it to us." || 4 ||
Then that <s>Dharmarāja</s>, righteous-souled, firm in righteousness,
having heard these words of those whose compassionate disposition had been destroyed, said: || 5 ||

children.text: kim etat kathyatāṃ śīghraṃ katham etat punar bruvan |
children.translated_text: "What is this? Speak quickly! How can this be?" And they said again:
then those terrible servants of <s>Yama</s>, to the wicked beings, || 6 ||
spoke these words to <s>Yama</s> the <s>Dharmarāja</s>:
"O Lord, this great being has been born in the confines of hell, || 7 ||

children.text: avīcir yasya nāmedaṃ tenāsau saṃkaṭa ucyate |
children.translated_text: in that which is called <s>Avīci</s> — therefore it is called 'confine' (saṃkaṭa);

children.text: karmaṇāṃ yasya vaicitryaṃ sattvā yena sukhīkṛtāḥ || 8 ||
children.translated_text: through the wonder of whose <s>karmas</s> (deeds), beings have been made happy. || 8 ||

children.text: sukhito hy eṣa sarvatra punar yāsyati surālayam |
children.translated_text: He, being happy everywhere, will again go to the abode of the gods."

children.text: yamo 'pi dharmarājā vai dṛṣṭvā kathayati vismitaḥ || 9 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s>, the <s>Dharmarāja</s> too, having seen, spoke in amazement: || 9 ||
"This one is of great supernatural power, and great is his body from a former birth;

children.text: yathā dhātuśatair vṛndaiḥ stūpaṃ śobhati śāstunaḥ || 10 ||
children.translated_text: just as the <s>stūpa</s> (reliquary) of the Teacher shines with hundreds of relics, || 10 ||

body.text: tathāsya śobhate kāyaḥ pratisarābaddhakaṇṭhakaḥ |
body.translated_text: so shines the body of this one, with the <s>Pratisarā</s> bound at his neck."

children.text: atha te narakapālakā yakṣā yamasya dharmarājasyedaṃ vacanam abruvan | katham idaṃ deva pratisarety ucyate | dharmarāja uvāca |
children.translated_text: Then those hell-guardian <s>yakṣas</s> spoke these words to <s>Yama</s> the <s>Dharmarāja</s>: "How is it, O Lord, that this is called '<s>Pratisarā</s>'?" The <s>Dharmarāja</s> said:

children.text: pratipat smārayed yas tu sa na gacchati durgatim |
children.translated_text: "He who makes others remember the [right] path — he does not go to a bad destiny;
he goes to a good destiny, being imbued with the nature of <s>Pratisarā</s>. || 11 ||
Or else, O hell-guardians, go to <s>Puṣkalāvatī</s>;
there you will see a great shrine, surrounded by deities. || 12 ||

body.text: tad dṛṣṭvā sarvasattveṣu maitracittā bhaviṣyatha |
body.translated_text: Having seen that, you will become benevolent-minded toward all beings.

children.translated_text: [Section 23]

children.text: atha te yamapuruṣā tasyām eva rātryāṃ puṣkalāvatīṃ gatāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then those servants of <s>Yama</s> went that very night to <s>Puṣkalāvatī</s>.
They then saw there, near the royal capital,
that mansion completely enveloped in a single blaze of flame. (13)
And they see the dead body with a <s>Pratisarā</s> [amulet] tied around its neck,
[surrounded] by gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, and <s>kiṃnaras</s>, (14)

body.text: parivāritaṃ samantena pūjāṃ kurvanty anuttarām |
body.translated_text: encircled on all sides, performing supreme worship.

children.translated_text: [Section 24]

children.text: yāvat tasya tair yakṣaiḥ pratisarakūṭo nāma sthāpitaḥ | atha te yakṣāḥ punar āgatya yamasya dharmarājasya niścayaṃ vistareṇārocayanti sma | evam etad deva yathā tvayābhihitam | samanantarārocite 'smin vacanaparyavasāne sa mahāsattvas taṃ nārakaṃ śarīraṃ vijahya trayastriṃśeṣu deveṣūpapannaḥ | tena hetunā pratisarapūrvī devaputra ity ucyate |
children.translated_text: As long as by those <s>yakṣas</s> the <s>Pratisara</s> peak was established in his name, those <s>yakṣas</s>, having returned, reported in detail the decision to <s>Yama</s>, the King of <s>Dharma</s>: 'So it is, O god, as you have stated.' Immediately upon this report, at the conclusion of those words, that great being abandoned that hellish body and was reborn among the Thirty-Three Gods (<s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>). For that reason, the one who formerly [bore] the <s>Pratisarā</s> is called a 'son of the gods' (<s>devaputra</s>).
[Section 25]

children.text: tena hi mahābrāhmaṇa parijñātapūrvam | tasmād avaśyam eveyaṃ mahāpratisareti dhārayitavyā vācayitavyā likhitavyā yathāvidhinā nityaṃ śarīragatāṃ kṛtvā dhārayitavyā | sa nityaṃ sarvavyasanaduḥkhebhyaḥ parimucyate | sarvadurgatibhayabhairavebhya uttarati | na ca vidyutā śakyaṃ pātayitum | kim iti vidyutā parijñātapūrvam |
children.translated_text: For this has been known previously, O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. Therefore, this <s>Mahāpratisarā</s> must certainly be held, recited, written, and, according to the proper rites, always kept on the body. One is always liberated from all calamities and sufferings. One crosses beyond all fears and terrors of evil destinies. And one cannot be struck down by lightning. Why? Because [its power against] lightning has been known previously.
[Section 26]

children.text: mahābrāhmaṇa hiṅgumardane mahānagaravare vimalaśaṅkho nāma śreṣṭhī mahādhanakanakasamṛddhaḥ paripūrṇakośakoṣṭhāgārasaṃpanno babhūva | sārthavāha iti khyātavān | atha sa mahāsārthavāho yānapātram āsādya mahāsamudre 'vatīrṇaḥ | yāvat timiṅgilaiḥ so 'sya poto 'vaṣṭabdhaḥ | vināśayitukāmā nāgāś ca saṃkṣubdhā mahāntaṃ garjanāsphoṭaṃ kurvanti vidyudulkām utsṛjanti vajrāśaniṃ pravarṣitum ārabdhāḥ | tatas te vaṇijo mahatā duḥkhenābhyāhatacittās taṃ mahāntaṃ nāgasaṃkṣobhaṃ vidyudulkāṃ vajrāśaniṃ cotsṛjantaṃ taiś ca timiṅgilaiḥ potam avaṣṭabdhaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahāntam utkrośanāśabdaṃ kartum ārabdhāḥ | te devatāviśeṣān āyācayanti | na ca kaścit teṣāṃ paritrāṇaṃ bhavati | tatas te sārthavāhasyopagamya karuṇakaruṇam idaṃ vacanam abruvan |
children.translated_text: O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, in the great city of <s>Hiṅgumardana</s>, there was a merchant named <s>Vimalaśaṅkha</s>, greatly prosperous with wealth and gold, with storehouses and granaries fully stocked. He was known as a caravan leader. Then that great caravan leader, having obtained a ship, descended into the great ocean. Thereupon his boat was seized by great whales (<s>timiṅgila</s>). Hostile <s>nāgas</s>, desiring to destroy it, stirred up greatly, making great thundering and roaring, releasing lightning bolts, and began to rain down thunderbolts (<s>vajrāśani</s>). Then those merchants, their minds struck by great suffering, seeing the great disturbance of the <s>nāgas</s> releasing lightning bolts and thunderbolts, and the boat seized by those whales, began to make a great wailing sound. They supplicated various deities, but no one came to their rescue. Then they approached the caravan leader and spoke these most piteous words:
'Save us, O great being! Free us from this great peril!'
Then the great caravan leader, firm-minded, of great wisdom, (1)
spoke these words to the distressed merchants:

children.text: mā bhair mā bhair vaṇijo bhavanto dhīratāṃ vrajata || 2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Fear not! Fear not, O merchants! Take courage! (2)'
'I shall free you from this great ocean of suffering.'

children.text: tato dhīramanaso bhūtvā vaṇija idaṃ vacanam abruvan || 3 ||
children.translated_text: Then, having become steadfast in mind, the merchants spoke these words: (3)

children.text: kim etan mahāsattva brūhi śīghram avighnataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'What is this [means], O great being? Tell us quickly, without delay!'
'Our lives [depend] on your power, O great-minded one! (4)'

children.text: kathyatāṃ jñānamāhātmyaṃ paścāt tvaṃ kiṃ kariṣyasi |
children.translated_text: 'Tell us the greatness of the knowledge! Then what will you do?'

children.text: tataḥ sārthapatis teṣām imāṃ vidyām udāharat || 5 ||
children.translated_text: Then the caravan leader proclaimed this <s>vidyā</s> (spell) to them: (5)
'I possess a great <s>vidyā</s> (spell), renowned by the name <s>Pratisarā</s>,'
'the subduer of all evil ones, of great strength and prowess. (6)'

body.text: tenāhaṃ mocayiṣyāmi atiduḥkhamahābhayāt |
body.translated_text: 'By that [spell] I shall free [you] from the great peril of extreme suffering.'

children.translated_text: [Section 27]

children.text: tataḥ sa mahāsārthavāhas tasyāṃ velāyām imāṃ mahāpratisarāṃ mahāvidyārājñīṃ likhitvā dhvajāgrāvaropitāṃ kārayati sma | samanantaradhvajāgrāvaropite 'smin mahāpratisare sarva eva te timiṅgilās tat potam ekajvālībhūtaṃ paśyanti | tatas te nāgā maitramanasas teṣām antike 'vatīrya pūjāṃ kartum ārabdhāḥ | te ca timiṅgilā asyā eva mahāpratisarāvidyārājñyā anubhāvena dahyamānā niṣpalāyitā vilayaṃ gatās te ca sārthikās tair mahānāgair mahati mahāratnadvīpe prāpitā iti |
children.translated_text: Then that great caravan leader, at that very moment, wrote this <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s> and had it raised on the top of a banner-staff. The moment this <s>Mahāpratisarā</s> was raised on the banner-top, all those whales (<s>timiṅgila</s>) saw the boat as a single mass of flame. Thereupon those <s>nāgas</s>, becoming benevolent-minded, descended near them and began to perform worship. And those whales, being burned by the power of this very <s>Mahāpratisarā Vidyārājñī</s>, fled and disappeared. And those caravan merchants were brought by those great <s>nāgas</s> to a great island of precious jewels.
[Section 28]

children.text: jñānavatī mahāvidyā mahāpratisarā sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhitā | tena hetuneyaṃ mahābrāhmaṇa mahāvidyeti khyātā | avaśyam eveyaṃ dhvajāgrāvaropitāṃ kṛtvā dhārayitavyā | sarvavātaśītākālameghavidyudaśaniṃ praśamayati | sarvadevamanuṣyāmanuṣyavigrahavivādeṣu parimocayati | sarvadaṃśamaśakaśalabhaprāṇakajātā vividharūpāḥ sasyavināśakā na prabhavanti | praśamaṃ gacchanti | sarve ca duṣṭacittā mṛgapakṣiṇo daṃṣṭriṇo vinaśyanti | sarvāṇi ca puṣpaphalapattravanaspatyoṣadhisasyādīny abhivardhante | surasāni svādūni mṛdūni ca bhaviṣyanti | samyag eva paripācitāni bhaviṣyanti | ativṛṣṭyanāvṛṣṭidoṣāḥ sarveṇa sarvaṃ na bhaviṣyanti | kālavṛṣṭir bhaviṣyati nākālavṛṣṭiḥ | ye ca tasmin viṣaye mahānāgās te ca samyag eva kālena kālaṃ varṣadhārā utsṛjanti | yasmin viṣaye iyaṃ mahāvidyārājñī mahāpratisarā nāma pracariṣyati tatra taiḥ sattvair jñātvā pūjāsatkāraṃ kṛtvā nānāgandhair nānādhūpair nānāpuṣpair nānāvastraiḥ pariveṣṭayitvā caityasyopari dhvajāgrāvaropitāṃ kṛtvā nānāvādyatūryasaṃgītibhir vādyamānābhiḥ pradakṣiṇīkartavyā | teṣāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ yathācintitam āśāṃ paripūrayiṣyanti devatāḥ śakrabrahmaprabhṛtayaḥ | athavā yathā yathā vidhinā likhyate tathā tathā samṛdhyate |
children.translated_text: Endowed with knowledge is this great <s>vidyā</s>, the <s>Mahāpratisarā</s>, blessed by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. For that reason, O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, this is known as the great <s>vidyā</s>. It must certainly be held by raising it on a banner-top. It pacifies all wind, cold, unseasonable clouds, lightning, and thunderbolts. It liberates from all conflicts and disputes among gods, humans, and non-humans. All kinds of gadflies, mosquitoes, locusts, and various creatures that destroy crops are unable to prevail — they are pacified. All evil-minded animals, birds, and fanged creatures perish. All flowers, fruits, leaves, trees, herbs, and crops flourish. They become juicy, sweet, and tender. They will be properly ripened. Faults of excessive rain and drought will not occur at all. Rain will fall in season, not out of season. And the great <s>nāgas</s> in that region will release rain-showers properly and in due time. In whatever region this great <s>Vidyārājñī</s> named <s>Mahāpratisarā</s> will be practiced, there those beings, having known [it] and performed worship and honor with various perfumes, various incenses, various flowers, and various garments, having wrapped it and raised it on the top of a banner at a <s>caitya</s> (shrine), it should be circumambulated with various instrumental music and songs. The deities, beginning with <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s>, will fulfill the wishes of those great beings as they have thought. Moreover, in whatever manner it is written according to the rites, in that manner it succeeds.
One desiring a son obtains a son; [it is] supreme in sustaining pregnancy.

children.text: sukhena vardhate garbhaḥ sukhena ca prasūyate || 1 ||
children.translated_text: The embryo grows with ease and is delivered with ease. (1)

body.text: kālena vardhate garbhaḥ kālena parimucyate |
body.translated_text: The embryo grows in due time and is released in due time.

children.translated_text: [Section 29]
Why, O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>? Let it be heard as before.

body.text: ihaiva magadhaviṣaye rājā prasāritapāṇir nāmnā | sa cāputrako babhūva | kim iti prasāritapāṇir iti khyātavān | tena rājñā jātamātreṇa pāṇiṃ prasārya mātuḥ stanaṃ gṛhītvā yāvad āptaṃ kṣīraṃ pītam | tau ca stanau sahasparśamātreṇa suvarṇavarṇau saṃvṛttau | nityakālaṃ ca mahākṣīreṇa pravardhate | tena kāraṇena rājñaḥ prasāritapāṇir iti nāma sthāpitam abhūt | anyac ca tasya rājño yadā yācanakajanā āgacchanti tadā sa rājā dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇiṃ prasārayaty antarīkṣe | bodhisattvaḥ sa rājā tena hetunā tasya buddhābhiprasannā devatā divyai ratnaviśeṣaiḥ suvarṇamaṇibhiś ca pāṇiṃ paripūrayanti | sa rājā tebhyo yācanakajanapadebhyo 'nuprayacchati | yathācintitamātreṇa sarvayācanakānāṃ sarvasukhasaṃpattikāmān dadāti | devānāṃ ca mahānti mahāpūjāsatkārāṇi karoti putrahetor na ca putraṃ pratilabhate | sa paurāṇāṃ tathāgatacaityānāṃ punaḥ punaḥ satkāraṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ | mahānti pūjāsatkārāṇi karoti | dānāni dadāti | upavāsam upavasati | mahānti puṇyāni karoti | akṣīṇāny eva dānāni dadāti | tat kasya hetoḥ |
body.translated_text: Here in this very <s>Magadha</s> region, there was a king named <s>Prasāritapāṇi</s> ('Extended Hand'). And he was childless. Why was he known as <s>Prasāritapāṇi</s>? Because that king, as soon as he was born, extended his hand and grasped his mother's breast and drank the milk to his fill. And both those breasts turned golden in color at the mere touch. And he always grew nourished by abundant milk. For that reason, the name <s>Prasāritapāṇi</s> was established for the king. Furthermore, when supplicants came to that king, the king would extend his right hand into the sky. He was a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, that king; for that reason, the deities pleased with the <s>Buddha</s> would fill his hand with divine precious jewels and gold and gems. The king would then distribute to those supplicant peoples. By the mere thought of a wish, he gave all happiness and prosperity desired by all supplicants. And he performed great worship and honor for the gods, for the sake of a son, yet he did not obtain a son. He began to repeatedly perform honor for the ancient <s>Tathāgata</s> shrines (<s>caitya</s>). He performed great worship and honor. He gave gifts. He observed fasts. He performed great meritorious deeds. He gave inexhaustible gifts. For what reason?

children.translated_text: [Section 30]

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ mahābrāhmaṇa asminn eva magadhaviṣaye mallā nāma janapade kuśinagare mahāpattanavare bhagavataḥ prabhūtaratnasya śāsane samutpanno dharmacittakaḥ kaścin mahāsattvo dharmamatir nāma śreṣṭhī prativasati | sa sarvasattvānām antike mahākaruṇācittam upasthāpyemām eva mahāvidyāṃ mahāpratisarām ārabhya dharmaṃ deśayati | atha kaścid eva daridrapuruṣas taṃ dharmaṃ śrutvā tasya mahāśreṣṭhina idaṃ vacanam abravīt | aham āryasya niveśane bhṛtikarma kariṣyāmi dharmaṃ ca śroṣyāmi | yadā mama kiṃcid bhaviṣyati tadāhaṃ dharmaṃ pūjayiṣyāmi | tasya gṛhavyāpāraṃ kurvato dharmaṃ ca śṛṇvato apareṇa samayena tena śreṣṭhinā tasyaikaṃ dīnāraṃ dattam | tena sarvasattvaparitrāṇārthaṃ bodhicittam utpādya sarvasattvasādhāraṇaṃ kṛtvā mahāpratisararatneti niryātitam | evaṃ ca praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam | anena dānamahāphalena mama sarvasattvānāṃ ca dāridryasamucchedaḥ syāt | tena kāraṇena tad dānaṃ parikṣayaṃ na gacchati |
children.translated_text: Formerly, O great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, in this very <s>Magadha</s> region, in the district called <s>Mallā</s>, in the great city of <s>Kuśinagara</s>, during the dispensation of the Blessed <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, there arose one who had generated the thought of <s>Dharma</s>—a certain great being, a merchant named <s>Dharmamati</s>, who dwelt there. He, having aroused great compassion toward all beings, taught the <s>Dharma</s> concerning this very <s>Mahāvidyā Mahāpratisarā</s>. Then a certain poor man, having heard that <s>Dharma</s>, spoke these words to that great merchant: 'I shall do hired labor in the noble one's house and listen to the <s>Dharma</s>; when I have something, then I shall make offerings to the <s>Dharma</s>.' While he was doing household work and listening to the <s>Dharma</s>, after some time the merchant gave him one <s>dīnāra</s> (gold coin). He, having generated <s>bodhicitta</s> (the thought of awakening) for the protection of all beings and making it shared with all beings, offered it as 'the jewel of <s>Mahāpratisarā</s>.' And he made this aspiration: 'By the great fruit of this gift, may the poverty of myself and all beings be completely eradicated.' For that reason, that gift never comes to exhaustion.

children.text: evaṃ bahuvidhānekavidhaḥ puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ kṛto devatāś ca pūjitā yāvanto buddhā bhagavantaḥ pūjitās tadā śuddhāvāsakāyikābhir devatābhiḥ svapne darśanaṃ dattam evaṃ cābhihitam | bho mahārāja samantajvālāmālāviśuddhisphuritacintāmaṇimudrāhṛdayāparājitā mahādhāraṇī vidyārājñī mahāpratisarā nāma | yathāvidhinālikhya yathāvidhinā kalpo 'bhihita upavāsoṣitāyā yathāvidhinā agramahiṣyā devyāḥ śarīre baddhvā tatas te putrapratilābho bhaviṣyati | atha sa rājā prativibuddhas tasyā rātryā atyayena saṃkhyālipinakṣatragrahavipañcakān kulabrāhmaṇān saṃnipātya yathāvidhinā kalpopadiṣṭe puṣyanakṣatrarāje pratipanne susnātagātrāyā upavāsoṣitāyā agramahiṣyā devyā yathāvidhinālikhyemāṃ mahāpratisarāṃ vidyārājñīṃ kaṇṭhe baddhavān | mahatīṃ mahābuddhacaityeṣu pūjām akārṣīt | anekāni ca ratnaviśeṣāni sattvānāṃ dānāni dattāni | tato navānāṃ māsānām atyayāt putro jātaḥ | abhirūpaḥ prāsādiko darśanīyaḥ paramayā śubhavarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgataḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus various and manifold accumulations of merit were made and deities were honored; and as many Buddhas and Blessed Ones were worshipped, then the deities of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abodes) gave a vision in a dream and spoke thus: 'O great king, the <s>Mahāpratisarā</s> is named the invincible great <s>dhāraṇī</s>, queen of spells, the heart-seal of the <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem), radiant with the splendor of all-encompassing flaming garlands of purity. Having written it according to the prescribed rite, and the ritual having been proclaimed according to the rite, having the chief queen observe a fast according to the rite, bind it upon the body of the queen—then you shall obtain a son.' Then that king, having awakened, after the passing of that night, assembled <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> of good family skilled in numbers, scripts, asterisms, planets, and the five [sciences], and according to the prescribed ritual, when the royal <s>Puṣya</s> asterism was attained, he had the <s>Mahāpratisarā Vidyārājñī</s> written according to the rite and bound it on the neck of the chief queen, who had bathed well and observed a fast. He made a great offering at the great Buddha <s>caityas</s> (shrines). And many kinds of special jewels were given as gifts to beings. Then, after the passing of nine months, a son was born—handsome, dignified, pleasing to behold, endowed with supreme beauty of complexion.

children.text: iti jñātvā mahābrāhmaṇa sarvakāmaṃgamāparājitā mahāpratisararatneti viśrutā mahāvidyārājñī sarvatathāgatapūjitā | śakrasyāpīyaṃ cūḍāmaṇiḥ sarvathā |
children.translated_text: Thus know, O great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>: this great <s>Vidyārājñī</s> (Queen of Spells), invincible, fulfilling all desires, renowned as 'the jewel of <s>Mahāpratisarā</s>,' is worshipped by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. She is in every way the crest-jewel even of <s>Śakra</s>.

children.text: yadā śakro devendro mahāsaṃgrāmam asuraiḥ sārdhaṃ kartukāmas tadā imām eva kavacaṃ kṛtvā cūḍāyām avasthāpya sarvāsurān nirjitya parājitya sukhaṃ svastinā kṣemena devapuraṃ praviśati | sarvāsurair adhṛṣyo bhavati |
children.translated_text: When <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>Devas</s>, wishes to wage a great battle with the <s>Asuras</s>, he makes this very [spell] his armor, places it on his crest, and having conquered and defeated all the <s>Asuras</s>, enters the city of the gods happily, safely, and securely. He becomes unassailable by all <s>Asuras</s>.

children.text: evaṃ hi mahābrāhmaṇa prathamacittotpādam upādāya bodhisattvasyemāṃ mahāpratisarāṃ mahāvidyārājñīṃ dhārayataḥ sarvamārair anavamṛdyatā bhavati | yasyaiṣā kāyakaṇṭhagatā bhaviṣyati sa sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhito bhaviṣyati | sarvabodhisattvasaṃrakṣito bhaviṣyati | sarvadevamanuṣyarājarājāmātyabrāhmaṇagṛhapatibhiś ca satatasamitaṃ vanditaḥ pūjitaḥ saṃmānito bhaviṣyati | sarvadevāsuragaruḍakiṃnaramahoragābhyarcitaḥ pūjito bhaviṣyati | sa mahāsattva ity uvāca bhagavān mārabalapramardakaḥ | sarvavyādhivigato bhaviṣyati | sarvetyupadravopasargāś cāsya praśāmyanti | tasya mahāsattvasya sarvaśokavigamo bhaviṣyati | sarvadevatāś cāsya satatasamitaṃ rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ saṃvidhāsyanti |
children.translated_text: Thus, O great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, from the very first arising of <s>bodhicitta</s>, for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who bears this <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s>, there is immunity from being trampled by all <s>Māras</s>. Whoever shall have this upon their body or neck shall be empowered by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, protected by all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and shall be constantly venerated, honored, and respected by all gods, humans, kings, royal ministers, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and householders. That one shall be worshipped and honored by all <s>Devas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kiṃnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s>. That great being—so spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>—is a crusher of <s>Māra</s>'s army. That one shall be free from all diseases, and all calamities, misfortunes, and afflictions shall be pacified. That great being shall be freed from all sorrow. And all deities shall constantly provide protection, shelter, and guardianship to that one.

children.text: imāni cānena catvāry aparājitāmahāmantrahṛdayāni satatasamitaṃ likhitvā kāyagatāni kṛtvā dhārayitavyāni satatasamitaṃ manasikartavyāni svādhyāyitavyāni bhāvayitavyāni cādhyāśayena | sarvaduḥsvapnadurnimittāmaṅgalyabhāvā vinaśyanti sarvasukhasaṃpattayaś ca prādurbhaviṣyanti |
children.translated_text: And these four invincible great <s>mantra</s>-hearts should be constantly written, placed upon the body, and borne; they should be constantly kept in mind, recited, and meditated upon with a devoted intention. All bad dreams, ill omens, and inauspicious states shall be destroyed, and all forms of happiness and prosperity shall manifest.

body.text: atra mantrapadāḥ siddhāḥ sarvakarmakarāḥ śubhāḥ |
body.translated_text: Here are the accomplished <s>mantra</s> syllables, auspicious, performing all works:

body.text: oṃ amṛtavare vara 2 pravaraviśuddhe hūṃ 2 phaṭ 2 svāhā |
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ amṛtavare vara vara pravaraviśuddhe hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā</s>.

body.text: oṃ amṛtavilokini garbhasaṃrakṣaṇi ākarṣaṇi hūṃ 2 phaṭ 2 svāhā |
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ amṛtavilokini garbhasaṃrakṣaṇi ākarṣaṇi hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā</s>.

body.text: aparājitāhṛdayam |
body.translated_text: The heart of <s>Aparājitā</s> (the Invincible):

body.text: oṃ vimale jayavare amṛte hūṃ 2 phaṭ 2 svāhā |
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ vimale jayavare amṛte hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā</s>.

body.text: oṃ bhara 2 saṃbhara indriyabalaviśodhani hūṃ 2 phaṭ 2 ruru cale svāhā |
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ bhara bhara saṃbhara indriyabalaviśodhani hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ ruru cale svāhā</s>.

body.text: upahṛdayavidyā |
body.translated_text: The subsidiary heart-<s>vidyā</s>:

children.text:
aśeṣaiḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvaiś ca ekasaṃnipāte ekasvaranirghoṣeṇa imāni dhāraṇīmantrapadāni bhāṣitāni | mahāpratisarāmahāvidyārājñīhṛdayakavacāny etāni mantrapadāni sarvatathāgatamudrayā mudritāni | atidurlabham apy eṣāṃ śravaṇaṃ kiṃ punar likhanapaṭhanavācanadhāraṇaparadeśanā | buddhakṛtyam etad iti jñātavyam | iyaṃ hy atīva sarvatathāgataiḥ praśaṃsitānumoditā vyākṛtā | paramadurlabheyaṃ mahādhāraṇī | aparājitā mahāpratisarā | nāmadheyam api paramadurlabhaṃ sarvapāpakṣayaṃkarī mahābalaparākramā mahātejā mahāprabhāvā mahāguṇodbhāvanī sarvamārakāyikadevatāvidhvaṃsanakarī sarvavāsanānusaṃdhimārapāśacchedanakarī | paramantramudrāviṣakākhordacūrṇakiraṇaprayogavidveṣaṇābhicārukāṇāṃ ca duṣṭacittānāṃ vidhvaṃsanakarī | buddhabodhisattvāryagaṇavarapūjābhiratānāṃ paripālanakarī |
mahāyānodgrahaṇalikhanavācanapaṭhanasvādhyāyanaśravaṇadhāraṇābhiyuktānāṃ paripālikeyaṃ mahādhāraṇī | yāvadbuddhabodhiparipūrayitrīyaṃ mahābrāhmaṇa mahāpratisarā vidyārājñī na kvacit pratihanyate | sarvatra ca mahāpūjāṃ prāpnoti yathāhaṃ śāstā jitavidviṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: By all the Buddhas and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> without exception, assembled in one gathering, with a single voice and resonance, these <s>dhāraṇī</s>-<s>mantra</s> syllables were spoken. These <s>mantra</s> syllables are the heart-armor of the <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s>, sealed with the seal of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Even the hearing of these is exceedingly rare, how much more so the writing, reading, reciting, bearing, and teaching to others! This should be known as the work of a Buddha. This [<s>dhāraṇī</s>] is supremely praised, approved, and prophesied by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. This great <s>dhāraṇī</s> is supremely rare—the invincible <s>Mahāpratisarā</s>. Even her name is supremely rare—she who destroys all sins, of great power and valor, of great energy, of great efficacy, who manifests great virtues, who annihilates all deities of <s>Māra</s>'s retinue, who severs the bonds of <s>Māra</s> that follow all latent tendencies. She who destroys the evil-minded ones who practice hostile <s>mantras</s>, seals, poisons, <s>kākhordas</s> (sorcery), powders, magical projections, discord-sowing, and destructive rites. She who protects those who delight in the worship of the Buddhas, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and the noble assembly. This great <s>dhāraṇī</s> protects those who are devoted to the taking up, writing, reciting, reading, self-study, hearing, and bearing of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. O great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, this <s>Mahāpratisarā Vidyārājñī</s>, which brings to fulfillment the <s>Bodhi</s> of the Buddha, is never obstructed anywhere. And she obtains great worship everywhere, just as I, the Teacher, conqueror of adversaries [receive worship].

children.text: kim iti | pūrvaṃ parijñātavatīyaṃ mahāvidyā sarvavighnavināyakānāṃ vidhvaṃsayitrī |
children.translated_text: Why so? Because this great <s>vidyā</s>, which was formerly fully comprehended, destroys all <s>Vighnavināyakas</s> (obstacle-creating beings).

body.text: yadā ca bhagavān vipulaprahasitavadanamaṇikanakaratnojjvalaraśmiprabhāsābhyudgatarājas tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ prathamābhisaṃbuddho yena bodhimaṇḍas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ sarvabuddhapraśastaṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartayitukāmas tadā tasya bhagavataḥ sarvamāraiḥ saparivārair anekamārakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparivṛtair nānārūpavirūpabhayabhairavaśabdākulair bahuvividhamāraviṣayavikurvaṇādhiṣṭhānair nānāpraharaṇavṛṣṭim abhinirmāyāgatya caturdiśaṃ parivāryānantāparyantamārakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrātirekāḥ pāpīyāṃso antarāyaṃ kartum ārabdhāḥ | tataḥ sa bhagavān vipulaprahasitavadanamaṇikanakaratnojjvalaraśmiprabhāsābhyudgatarājo muhūrtaṃ tūṣṇīm āsthāya imāṃ mahāpratisarāṃ mahāvidyāṃ manasā saptakṛtvaḥ pravartayām āsa | samanantarapravartite 'smin mahāpratisare vidyārāje tatkṣaṇād eva sarve te mārāḥ pāpīyāṃso dadṛśur bhagavata ekaikasmād romavivarād anekakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi saṃnaddhabaddhakavacānāṃ jvalitakhaḍgaparaśupāśamudgarāsitriśūlahastānām evaṃ vācaṃ pravyāharamāṇāni nirgacchanti | gṛhnata 2 bandhata 2 duṣṭamārāṃ vidhvaṃsayata duṣṭacittānāṃ vicūrṇayata jīvitaṃ sarvaduṣṭagrahavighnavināyakānāṃ ye bhagavato viheṭhāṃ kurvanti | tatas te sarvaduṣṭamārān maitrīkhaḍgenābhinirjitān kṛtvā kecic chikṣāpadāni grāhitāḥ kecid yāvad anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau vyākṛtās tatra mahānubhāvāḥ | anye punas tāṃs tathāgataromavivaravinirgatān mahāpuruṣān dṛṣṭvā tasmin nagare vihvalībhūtā ṛddhiparihīnā pratibhānabalaparākramapranaṣṭā vidhvastāḥ samastāḥ prapalīnā iti | tato bhagavatā dharmacakraṃ pravartitaṃ yathānyair buddhair iti | sarvavighnavināyakān mārāṃś ca pāpīyāṃso vidhvaṃsayitvā uttīrṇaḥ pāraṃgataḥ |
body.translated_text: And when the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, the radiant king arisen with the splendor of rays blazing with jewels, gold, and gems from his vast smiling countenance — when he, having first attained supreme awakening, approached the seat of enlightenment (<s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>), wishing to turn the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of the Law) praised by all <s>Buddhas</s> — then all the <s>Māras</s> with their retinues, surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>Māras</s>, with terrifying sounds of various forms and monstrous appearances, with many varied magical displays and powers of the realm of <s>Māra</s>, with various weapons, assailed the Blessed One.

children.text: evaṃ hi mahābrāhmaṇa mahābalavegaṛddhipāramitāprāpteyaṃ mahāpratisarā mahāvidyārājñī smaraṇamātreṇa sarvavyasanabhayabhairavebhyaḥ parimocayati āśayapariśuddhānāṃ sattvānāṃ nānyeṣāṃ duṣṭacetasām | tasmāt tarhi mahābrāhmaṇa nityam evānusmaraṇena manasikāreṇa manasikartavyā | sarvakālaṃ ca likhitvā kāyagatāṃ kṛtvā dhārayitavyā |
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, O great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, this <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s> (Great Protectress, Great Queen of Spells), which has attained the perfection of great strength, speed, and supernatural power, liberates from all calamities, fears, and terrors by mere recollection — [but only] for beings whose intentions are purified, not for others of wicked mind. Therefore, O great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, it should always be brought to mind through constant recollection and mindful attention. And at all times, having written it down and placed it upon the body, it should be worn.
What is that? It is the word spoken previously.

body.text: ujjayanyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ rājño brahmadattasya vijite kenacit puruṣeṇāparādhaḥ kṛtaḥ | sa rājñā brahmadattena vadhakapuruṣebhya ājñaptaḥ | bhavanto gacchatainaṃ puruṣaṃ jīvitād vyaparopayatha | atha te vadhakapuruṣās taṃ rājñājñaptaṃ puruṣaṃ gṛhītvā parvatavivaraṃ gatvāsiṃ kośān niṣkāsya taṃ puruṣaṃ jīvitād vyavaropayitum ārabdhāḥ | tadā sa puruṣa imāṃ mahāpratisarāṃ mahāvidyārājñīṃ manasā smṛtavān | likhitāṃ ca dakṣine bāhau dhārayati sma | tasya mahāsattvasyāsyā mahāvidyāyāḥ prabhāvenāsir ekajvālībhūtā khaṇḍakhaṇḍaṃ yathā pāṃsumayo vikīrṇa iti | tatas te vadhakapuruṣā imam eva niścayaṃ rājño vistareṇārocayām āsuḥ | tato rājā prakupitaḥ kathayati | gacchatha bhoḥ puruṣā anyatamasmin pradeśe yakṣaguhāsti | tatra bahūni yakṣaśatasahasrāṇi prativasanti piśitāśinaḥ | tatra nītvā chorayata | tataḥ sa puruṣas tair vadhakapuruṣais tasyāṃ yakṣaguhāyāṃ choritaḥ | samanantarachorite tasmin yakṣaguhāyāṃ tatas te yakṣāḥ sarve tuṣṭamanasaḥ pradhāvitā mānuṣaṃ bhakṣayiṣyāma iti te paśyanti asyā mahāpratisarāyā anubhāvena taṃ puruṣam ekajvālāmālārciṣaṃ dedīpyamānaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca sarva eva saṃtrastā dahyamānaṃ śarīraṃ paśyanti | atha te yakṣā vismayam āpannās taṃ puruṣaṃ gṛhītvā bahirdvāre 'vasthāpya pradakṣiṇaṃ kartum ārabdhāḥ | yāvat tair vadhakapuruṣai rājño 'yaṃ niścayo vistareṇārocitaḥ | tato bhūyo rājā kupitaś caṇḍībhūtaḥ kathayati | yady evaṃ bhavanto gacchathainaṃ puruṣaṃ baddhvā nadyāṃ prakṣipatha | sa taiḥ puruṣair baddhvā nadyāṃ prakṣiptaḥ | samanantaraprakṣipte ca tasmin mahāpuruṣe sā nadī nirudakībhūtā yathā sa puruṣaḥ sthalagata eva tiṣṭhati | te ca bandhanāḥ khaṇḍakhaṇḍaṃ vicūrṇitāḥ | rājñā śrutam | tato rājā vismayotphullitavadanaḥ kathayati | aho vismayam idaṃ puruṣasya | kim atra kāraṇaṃ syād iti me vitarkaḥ | atha sa rājā taṃ puruṣaṃ āhūyaivam āha | kiṃ tvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa jānāsi | puruṣa uvāca | nāhaṃ mahārāja kiṃcid api jānāmi anyatra mahāpratisarāṃ mahāvidyāṃ dhārayāmi | tasyā eva deva prabhāvaḥ | rājā āha | aho āścaryaṃ mahat | mahāvidyā subhāṣitā |
body.translated_text: In the great city of <s>Ujjayinī</s>, in the realm of King <s>Brahmadatta</s>, a certain man had committed an offense. He was ordered by King <s>Brahmadatta</s> to the executioners: 'Go, sirs, and take the life of this man.' Then those executioners, having seized the man condemned by the king's command, went to a mountain cleft, drew their swords from their scabbards, and began to take his life. Then that man mentally recalled this <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s> (Great Protectress, Great Queen of Spells).

children.translated_text: She who bewilders the rod of death, empowered by all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the savior of all beings, the liberator from sickness and suffering. || 1 ||
The great <s>Vidyā</s> (spell) of great power, the liberator from untimely death,
spoken by the compassionate Lords, the remover of great disease. || 2 ||

children.text: tato rājñā prahṛṣṭamānasena mahāpratisarā mahāvidyārājñī pūjitābhinanditā | tasya puruṣasya paṭṭabandhaṃ kṛtvā svakasya janapadasya purastān nagarajyeṣṭhatāyām abhiṣeko dattaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then the king, with a delighted mind, honored and praised the <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s>. He bound a fillet upon that man and bestowed upon him the consecration of chief headman before [the people of] his own land.

children.text: evaṃ mahābrāhmaṇeyaṃ mahāpratisarā vidyārājñī sarvatra mahatīṃ pūjāṃ labhate | anatikramaṇīyā sarvaduṣṭacittaiḥ sattvaiḥ | pūrvam iyaṃ parijñātā mahāvidyārājñī na kvacit pratihanyate | tasmād avaśyaṃ kāyagatāṃ kṛtvā dhārayitavyā | api tu mahābrāhmaṇa sunakṣatreṇeyaṃ supraśastavidhānena likhitavyā | atha sa mahābrāhmaṇo 'tīvaprahṛṣṭamanā bhagavantaṃ pañcamaṇḍalakenābhipraṇamya praṣṭum ārabdhaḥ | kīdṛśena bhagavan vidhāneneyaṃ mahāvidyārājñī likhitavyā | bhagavān āha | śṛṇu mahābrāhmaṇa tvām ahaṃ vakṣye sarvasattvānukampayā |
children.translated_text: Thus, O great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, this <s>Mahāpratisarā Vidyārājñī</s> (Great Protectress, Queen of Spells) receives great worship everywhere. She cannot be transgressed by beings of wicked mind. When this great <s>Vidyārājñī</s> (Queen of Spells) has been previously understood, she is never obstructed anywhere. Therefore she must certainly be placed upon the body and worn. Moreover, O great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, this [spell] should be written under an auspicious constellation with a well-prescribed ritual. Then that great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, with an exceedingly delighted mind, having bowed to the Blessed One with the five-point prostration, began to ask: 'What [is the procedure]?'

children.text: yena sattvāḥ sukhino bhonti mucyante karmasaṃkaṭāt |
children.translated_text: By which beings become happy and are freed from the straits of <s>karma</s>;
for the liberation of the diseased, and for the safe delivery of women's pregnancy. || 1 ||
And there shall be for beings the healing of poverty and wounds;
having observed a fast, on the constellation approved as <s>Puṣya</s>, || 2 ||
being devoted to the worship of the <s>Buddha</s>, having generated the mind toward awakening (<s>Bodhi</s>),
with a mind infused with compassion and also endowed with loving-kindness, || 3 ||
and being always devoted to the welfare of all beings,
having bathed with sandalwood, camphor, and musk-water, || 4 ||
having put on clean garments fumigated with incense,
then having made a <s>maṇḍala</s> (ritual diagram) with clay and cow-dung, || 5 ||
and four full water-vessels, with a fifth in the center of the <s>maṇḍala</s>,

children.text: puṣpadhūpāś ca gandhāś ca dātavyātra mahārhāḥ || 6 ||
children.translated_text: flowers, incense, and fragrances of great value should be offered here. || 6 ||

children.text: dhūpanaṃ candanaṃ caiva spṛkkāgaru tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: Incense of sandalwood and also <s>spṛkkā</s> (a fragrant plant) and <s>agaru</s> (aloewood),
and five kinds of sugar and <s>turuṣka</s> (frankincense) should be given according to the ritual procedure. || 7 ||
Various kinds of flowers, according to the season and according to the rite,
well-adorned with all flowers, fruits, seeds, and fragrances. || 8 ||
With clarified butter, honey, and milk, with fire-offerings of rice-pudding and the like,
one should fill the offering-vessels, endowed with auspicious marks. || 9 ||
One should place [them] in the four directions, with the fifth in the center of the <s>maṇḍala</s>;
and shallow bowls filled with fragrance should be placed at the corners. || 10 ||
And four pegs of <s>Khadira</s> (acacia) wood, firmly bound,
the skilled one having wrapped [them] with five-colored thread. || 11 ||
Having measured these equally, one should bury [them] outside the <s>maṇḍala</s> (sacred circle);

children.text: evaṃ kṛte likhed vipra yad icchet siddhim ātmanaḥ || 12 ||
children.translated_text: having done thus, O <s>vipra</s> (learned one), one should write what one desires for one's own <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment). || 12 ||
One who seeks happiness should write it, having eaten pure food,

children.text: paṭe vā vastrabhūrje vānyatra vā yatra kutracit || 13 ||
children.translated_text: on cloth, or on bark-paper, or elsewhere, wherever it may be. || 13 ||

children.text: likhet strīṣu putrārthī samyag gorocanena vai |
children.translated_text: One desiring a son should write it properly with <s>gorocanā</s> (ox-bile pigment) on women,
and in the center one should make a child adorned with all ornaments. || 14 ||
One should hold in the left hand a vessel filled with jewels;
he should be made seated on a lotus, adorned with full bloom. || 15 ||
Jewel-necklaces, gold, and various gems especially;
and at the four corners, unconquerable mountains should be made. || 16 ||

children.text: evaṃ likhet prayatnena yad icchej jīvituṃ sukham |
children.translated_text: Thus one should write with effort, if one wishes to live happily;

children.text: kuṅkumena likhet vāpi puruṣānāṃ tu viśeṣataḥ || 17 ||
children.translated_text: or one should write with saffron, especially for men. || 17 ||
His desired aims are accomplished — there is no doubt in this;

children.text: nānārūpāś ca kartavyā mudrācihnāś ca padminī || 18 ||
children.translated_text: and various forms and <s>mudrā</s>-signs (seal-marks) and the lotus-bearer should be made. || 18 ||

children.text: dve padme athavā trīṇi catvāri pañca vā likhet |
children.translated_text: One should draw two lotuses, or three, or four, or five;

children.text: padmānāṃ ca tathā kuryāt kesarāṇi samantataḥ || 19 ||
children.translated_text: and on the lotuses one should make filaments all around. || 19 ||
One should make a fully blossomed lotus with a stem, bound with a ribbon;
one should make a trident-lotus, eight-cornered, bound with a ribbon. || 20 ||
Likewise a lotus with an axe, eight-petaled all around;

children.text: sakhaḍgaṃ padmaṃ kurvīta sa padmaṃ sitam eva ca || 21 ||
children.translated_text: one should make a lotus with a sword, and a white lotus as well. || 21 ||

children.text: śaṅkhaṃ padme tathā kuryāt sarvatra vidhivistaram iti |
children.translated_text: Likewise one should make a conch on a lotus, with elaborate ritual detail throughout;
the skilled one should have ritual signs made everywhere. || 22 ||
One should avoid childish forms where the mind becomes corrupted;
and a divine form should be made, adorned with various ornaments. || 23 ||
One should make a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) as <s>Vajradhara</s> (Vajra-holder), intent on threatening the wicked;
and one should draw the four great kings on the four sides. || 24 ||
For a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) should be drawn; for <s>kṣatriyas</s> (warriors), <s>Maheśvara</s>;
for <s>śūdras</s>, one should always draw the gentle lord of the wheel (<s>Cakrasvāmin</s>). || 25 ||
For <s>vaiśyas</s> (merchants), <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> and <s>Indra</s>, the lord of gods;
for a child, <s>Prajāpati</s> (Lord of Creatures), the great-minded one, should always be drawn. || 26 ||

children.text: śyāmavarṇā bhaved yā tu raudraṃ tasyāḥ samālikhet |
children.translated_text: For one who is dark-complexioned, one should draw a fierce [form];
for a fair one, one should always draw a form endowed with beauty and glory. || 27 ||
For a stout woman, <s>Māṇibhadra</s> should be drawn with effort;

children.text: kṛṣāyāṃ pūrṇabhadras tu mayā hy uktaṃ svayambhuvā || 28 ||
children.translated_text: for a thin woman, <s>Pūrṇabhadra</s> — thus I, the Self-born (<s>Svayambhū</s>), have spoken. || 28 ||

children.text: gurviṇyāś ca mahākālaṃ likhec ca brahmadevatām |
children.translated_text: And for a pregnant woman, one should draw <s>Mahākāla</s> and the deity <s>Brahmā</s>;
and others as previously stated, one should draw according to the rite. || 29 ||
Having thus written with effort, with ritual-prescribed actions,

children.text: dhārayet satataṃ kaṇṭhe bhadrakaṃ tasya bhaviṣyati || 30 ||
children.translated_text: one should constantly wear it at the neck — auspiciousness will come to him. || 30 ||
One should make a flame-tipped <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem) at the <s>vajra</s>-tip, placed on a lotus;

children.text: padmasya kesare pāśaṃ cakraṃ cāpi tathā param || 31 ||
children.translated_text: on the filament of the lotus, a noose, and likewise a wheel beyond. || 31 ||
Having drawn a <s>vajra</s> on a lotus, a mace placed on a lotus;

children.text: śaktiṃ likhet tathā padme yathā vidhiṣu dṛśyate || 32 ||
children.translated_text: one should draw a spear (<s>śakti</s>) likewise on a lotus, as seen in the ritual texts. || 32 ||
All the gems with flame-tips, filled with sparks;

children.text: paṭṭabaddhāś ca kartavyā yathā vidhiṣu kīrtitāḥ || 33 ||
children.translated_text: and they should be made bound with ribbons, as proclaimed in the ritual texts. || 33 ||

children.text: nāgāś ca phaṇinaḥ kāryā maṇijvālā navaśīrṣāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Nāgas</s> (serpents) with hoods should be made, with jewel-flames, nine-headed;
all these too, with effort, established with <s>vajras</s> at the heart. || 34 ||

children.text: pārthivānāṃ balaṃ nityaṃ sārthavāhaṃ likhed budhaḥ |
children.translated_text: For kings, the wise one should always draw an army-leader (<s>sārthavāha</s>);
and for all <s>vidyādharas</s> (spell-bearers), one should draw the <s>Vidyādevī</s> (Knowledge Goddess). || 35 ||
The moon and sun with <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), <s>Rāhu</s>, <s>Ketu</s>, and the eight planets;
one should draw [them], and for eunuchs and impotent ones, the attainment of a son will come about. || 36 ||
Having drawn assuredly according to the rite, all <s>siddhis</s> (accomplishments) will be attained;
therefore, with all effort, the wise person should wear it. || 37 ||
For this is the accomplisher of all <s>siddhis</s>, auspicious, destroyer of sins;
one attains the supreme state, as spoken by the Self-born (<s>Svayambhū</s>). || 38 ||

children.text: loke 'smin paramaṃ saukhyaṃ paraloke sukhaṃ param |
children.translated_text: In this world, supreme happiness; in the next world, supreme bliss;
his abode is in the divine realm, beginning with the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Heaven of the Thirty-Three). || 39 ||
In <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, beautiful and delightful, in a distinguished and esteemed family,
among distinguished <s>kṣatriyas</s>, among <s>brāhmaṇas</s> especially — || 40 ||

children.text: janma tasya mahātmasya vidyā sukhaṃ ca nityaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: the birth of that great soul, knowledge, and happiness are constant;

children.text: sarvabuddhair na śakyaṃ hi puṇyaskandhaṃ prakīrtitum || 41 ||
children.translated_text: even all the Buddhas cannot fully proclaim the mass of merit. || 41 ||
The merit that one who wears the <s>Pratisarā</s> attains —
the doors of hell are closed, all the doors of heaven are opened. || 42 ||
He will be endowed with the wealth of happiness, the great-minded one;

children.text: buddhāś ca bodhisattvāś ca āśvāsayanti ca nityaśaḥ || 43 ||
children.translated_text: and the Buddhas and <s>bodhisattvas</s> constantly reassure him. || 43 ||
Endowed with happiness in body, he will be of great strength;

children.text: yathāpi tad vai jinendroktaṃ cakravartī bhaviṣyati || 44 ||
children.translated_text: as spoken by the <s>Jinendra</s> (Victorious Lord), he will become a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch). || 44 ||
He will be a comfort to divine kings, a terror to the evil-minded;
and this will come about shortly for one to whom this <s>vidyā</s> is well-spoken. || 45 ||

children.text: nāsau hanyati śastreṇa na viṣeṇa na cāgninā |
children.translated_text: He is not killed by weapons, nor by poison, nor by fire;
nor is there untimely death for him — the sinful ones go far away. || 46 ||

children.text: darśanāt sparśanāc caiva śravaṇād eva sarvataḥ |
children.translated_text: By seeing, by touching, and by hearing from all sides,
<s>bhūta</s>-spirit possessions and disputes, and fear from water and fire, || 47 ||

children.text: mṛgā vyāḍāhayo nāgā vyādhayaś ca sudāruṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: wild animals, serpents, snakes, <s>nāgas</s>, and terrible diseases —

children.text: te sarve na bhaviṣyanti yeṣāṃ vidyā subhāṣitā || 48 ||
children.translated_text: none of these will afflict those for whom this <s>vidyā</s> is well-spoken. || 48 ||

children.text: sarvathā sarvamārais tu śṛṇu vakṣyāmi tattvataḥ |
children.translated_text: In every way, regarding all <s>māras</s> (demonic forces) — hear, I shall speak the truth:
they will be worthy of worship, for they are the foremost among all beings. || 49 ||

body.text: mahāvidyārājasyāyaṃ mahāpratisarasya kalpaḥ samāptaḥ |
body.translated_text: The ritual manual (<s>kalpa</s>) of this <s>Mahāvidyārāja</s> (Great King of Sacred Knowledge), the <s>Mahāpratisara</s>, is complete.

children.translated_text: Now I shall explain the ritual manual of the protective rite of the <s>vidyādhara</s> (knowledge-holder), out of compassion for all beings.
By this protective rite, great <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) will be attained;

children.text: yatra tatra kṛtā rakṣā bhavaty avadhyo na saṃśayaḥ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: wherever protection is established, one becomes invulnerable — there is no doubt. || 1 ||
Freedom from fear, freedom from fever, and the warding off of all planetary afflictions,
favorable <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), and the cutting of the web of <s>karma</s> (deeds) — || 2 ||
what has been badly eaten, badly transgressed, done by hosts of enemies,

children.text: duḥprekṣitaṃ durlikhitaṃ kākhordā ye ca dāruṇāḥ || 3 ||
children.translated_text: maliciously gazed upon, maliciously written, and the terrible <s>kākhordas</s> (sorceries) — || 3 ||
what has been done by powdered spells, and poisons consumed, and poisonous substances —

children.text: sarve tasya praśāmyanti rakṣāṃ dhārayate 'tra yaḥ || 4 ||
children.translated_text: all these are pacified for one who wears this protection here. || 4 ||
Counter-spells (<s>pratyaṅgirā</s>) rebound upon one who transgresses this <s>vidyā</s>;
and those terrible enemy armies, and fearsome adversaries — || 5 ||
all of them go to destruction, threatened by the curse of <s>Pratisarā</s>;

children.text: buddhā rakṣanti sarvajñā bodhisattvāś ca sūratāḥ || 6 ||
children.translated_text: the omniscient Buddhas protect, and the gentle <s>bodhisattvas</s>. || 6 ||
<s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary Buddhas) protect, and <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) of great austerity;

children.text: anye ca bahuvidhā bhūyo devā nāgā maharddhikāḥ || 7 ||
children.translated_text: and many other kinds — gods, <s>nāgas</s>, and those of great supernatural power — || 7 ||

children.text: rakṣāṃ kurvanti tasyeme asmin yuktasya nityaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: these all perform protection for one who is constantly engaged in this;
by the mere hearing of this <s>vidyā</s>-protection, which is unsurpassed, || 8 ||

children.text: nirbhayaṃ bhavati sarvatra ity evaṃ munir abravīt |
children.translated_text: fearlessness arises everywhere — thus the <s>Muni</s> (Sage) has spoken.

children.text: duḥsvapnā duṣkṛtā ye ca upasargā ye ca dāruṇāḥ || 9 ||
children.translated_text: Bad dreams, evil deeds, and terrible misfortunes, || 9 ||
those afflicted by diseases, seized by great illnesses and consumption (<s>rājayakṣman</s>),

children.text: anye ca bahuvidhā rogā gaṇḍalūtā vicarcikāḥ || 10 ||
children.translated_text: and many other kinds of diseases — boils, poisonous spider [bites], eczema, || 10 ||

children.text: ītayo dāruṇā ye ca grasante mānuṣīṃ prajām |
children.translated_text: and terrible calamities that devour human offspring,
supremely terrible harmers, aimed at the destruction of humans — || 11 ||

children.text: sarve te vinaśyanti rakṣā yatra mahābalā |
children.translated_text: all these perish where this mighty protection is;
and one for whom this protection has been performed is freed even when destined for execution. || 12 ||

children.text: yadi grastaḥ kālapāśena nītaś cāpi yamālayam |
children.translated_text: Even if seized by the noose of death and taken to the abode of <s>Yama</s>,
his lifespan will increase even by the mere writing of the <s>Pratisarā</s>. || 13 ||

children.text: parikṣīṇāyuṣo yas tu saptāhamṛta eva ca |
children.translated_text: One whose lifespan is exhausted and who has been dead for seven days —
by the mere writing [of this], this protection is unsurpassed. || 14 ||
Or by mere hearing, through the performance of the protective rite,
one attains all well-being and lives happily as desired. || 15 ||
Sixty-eight thousand <s>koṭī</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundreds,

children.text: trāyastriṃśāś ca ye devāḥ sarve śakrapurogamāḥ || 16 ||
children.translated_text: and the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, all led by <s>Śakra</s> — || 16 ||
they stand behind that being for the purpose of protection;
and the four world-guardians (<s>lokapālas</s>), and <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> of great strength — || 17 ||
together with hundreds of <s>vidyā</s>-families, they constantly perform protection;
<s>Soma</s>, <s>Sumanā</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, || 18 ||

children.text: yamaś ca māṇibhadraś ca baladevo mahābalaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s> and <s>Māṇibhadra</s>, <s>Baladeva</s> of great strength,
<s>Pūrṇabhadra</s> the great hero, and <s>Hārītī</s> with her children, || 19 ||
<s>Pañcāla</s> and <s>Pāñcika</s>, <s>Kārttikeya</s> the lord of hosts,

children.text: śrīr api ca mahādevī vaiśravaṇaś ca sarasvatī || 20 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune) too, the great goddess, and <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, and <s>Sarasvatī</s> — || 20 ||
<s>Śaṅkhinī</s>, <s>Puṣpadantī</s>, and likewise <s>Ekajaṭā</s> —

children.text: dhanyā etā mahāyakṣā rakṣāṃ kurvanti nityaśaḥ || 21 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dhanyā</s> — these great <s>Yakṣas</s> always provide protection. || 21 ||
The begetting of sons for the impotent, the growth and sustaining of the fetus,

children.text: rakṣeyaṃ mahatī tasya yāvaj jīvaṃ bhaviṣyati || 22 ||
children.translated_text: this great protection shall be his as long as he lives. || 22 ||
For men it always grants victory in terrible wars and battles;
by this the deities established in the <s>Dharma</s> become boon-givers. || 23 ||

children.text: athavā pāpavināśe tu likhanād eva mucyate |
children.translated_text: Or else, for the destruction of sin, one is liberated by merely writing [this spell];
the <s>Tathāgatas</s> look upon [such a person], and likewise the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. || 24 ||

children.text: yaśaś ca vardhate tasya puṇyam āyuś ca vardhate |
children.translated_text: His fame increases, his merit and lifespan increase;
and there shall be abundance of wealth and grain — there is no doubt. || 25 ||

children.text: sukhaṃ svapiti medhāvī sukhaṃ ca prativibudhyate |
children.translated_text: The wise one sleeps happily and awakens happily;
he is invincible by all enemies and by all hosts of beings. || 26 ||
For one engaged in battle, there is always victory;
when a <s>Vidyā</s> (spell) is being practiced, this protection is unsurpassed. || 27 ||

children.text: sukhaṃ ca sādhayed vidyāṃ vighno 'sya na bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: One accomplishes the <s>Vidyā</s> (spell) happily, and no obstacle shall befall him;
all ritual procedures succeed, having entered every <s>maṇḍala</s>. || 28 ||

children.text: kṣipraṃ ca samayajño 'sau bhavet sarvatra jātiṣu |
children.translated_text: Quickly he becomes a knower of the vow in all births;
he becomes a trusted keeper of the secret of the <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors). || 29 ||
Endowed with all auspiciousness, with all accomplishments fulfilling wishes —
by merely writing this [spell], all happiness is attained. || 30 ||
Having died happily, he becomes one destined for heaven;
in disputes, quarrels, and in exceedingly terrible conflicts, || 31 ||
he is freed from all fears, according to the word spoken by the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror);

children.text: sa nityaṃ jātismaro bhoti jātau jātau na saṃśayaḥ || 32 ||
children.translated_text: he always has memory of past births, in birth after birth — there is no doubt. || 32 ||
Kings become subject to him, along with the inner apartments and the great assembly;

children.text: sa mānyaś ca bhaven nityaṃ sādhubhir lokasaṃmataiḥ || 33 ||
children.translated_text: he shall always be honored by virtuous ones esteemed by the world. || 33 ||

children.text: sarveṣāṃ ca priyo bhavati ye devā ye ca mānuṣāḥ |
children.translated_text: He becomes dear to all — both gods and humans;

children.text: rakṣāṃ tasya kariṣyanti divārātrau na saṃśayaḥ || 34 ||
children.translated_text: they shall provide protection for him, day and night — there is no doubt. || 34 ||
Here the <s>mantra</s>-words are perfected, spoken by the Perfectly Awakened One.

body.text: namo buddhāya | namo dharmāya | namaḥ saṃghāya | namo bhagavate śākyamunaye mahākāruṇikāya tathāgatāyārhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya | namas tebhyaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhebhyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>! Homage to the <s>Dharma</s>! Homage to the <s>Saṃgha</s>! Homage to the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the greatly compassionate <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One! Homage to those Perfectly Awakened Ones!

children.translated_text: Having paid homage to them with devotion, for the increase of the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching,
I shall now proclaim, out of compassion for all beings: || 1 ||
This <s>Vidyā</s> (spell) of great power, of great strength and valor,
at whose mere utterance, on the <s>vajra</s>-seat of the sages, || 2 ||

children.text: mārāś ca mārakāyāś ca grahāḥ sarvavināyakāḥ |
children.translated_text: the <s>Māras</s> and <s>Māra</s>-hosts, the planetary demons and all obstacle-makers,

children.text: vighnāś ca santi ye kecit tatkṣaṇād vilayaṃ gatāḥ || 3 ||
children.translated_text: and whatever obstacles there are — all vanish in that instant. || 3 ||
The [<s>mantra</s>] is as follows:
