body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s> <s>giri giri</s>! <s>giriṇi</s>! O mountain-possessing one! O virtuous one! O sky-possessing one! O you purified by the sky! O you freed from sin! O sky! O surface of heaven! O sky-wanderer! O blazing peak! O you who wear a crown studded with jewels and pearls! O you of beautiful hair! O beautiful-faced one! O beautiful-eyed one! O golden one! O golden-fair one! O you of the past! O unborn one! O you of the future! O you of the present! Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s> of blazing radiance! O awakened one! O well-awakened one! O blessed one! O excellent protectress! O subtle one! O radiant one! O well-tamed one! O well-disciplined one! O excellent one! O blessed one! O auspicious one! O virtuous one! O you of excellent virtue! O stainless one! O you of victorious virtue! O fierce one! O wrathful one! O <s>vajra</s>-wrathful one! O greatly wrathful one! O terrible one! <s>Gandhārī</s>! <s>Gaurī</s>! <s>Caṇḍālī</s>! <s>Mātaṅgī</s>! <s>Varcasī</s>! <s>Sumatī</s>! <s>Pukkasī</s>! <s>Śavarī</s>! <s>Śāvarī</s>! <s>Śaṅkarī</s>! <s>Dramiḍī</s>! <s>Drāmiḍī</s>! <s>Raudriṇī</s>! O accomplisher of all aims! Smite, smite all enemies! Burn, burn all the wicked, the <s>Pretas</s>, <s>Piśācas</s>, <s>Ḍākinīs</s>, humans and non-humans! Cook, cook! Destroy the hearts, annihilate the lives of all malevolent seizing spirits! Destroy, destroy all my sins, O blessed one! Protect, protect me and all beings everywhere from all fears and calamities! Bind all the wicked! O destroyer of all offenses! O sun! O averter of the rod of death! O rod of honor! O proud one! O greatly proud one! <s>cale</s>! <s>ciṭi ciṭi</s>! <s>viṭi viṭi</s>! <s>niṭi niṭi</s>! <s>niṭini</s>! <s>tuṭe</s>! O terrible one! O heroic one! O you of excellent combat! <s>Caṇḍālī</s>! <s>Mātaṅgī</s>! O you who obstruct! O you of the lake! <s>Varcasī</s>! <s>Sumatī</s>! <s>Pukkasī</s>! <s>Śavarī</s>! <s>Śāvarī</s>! <s>Śaṅkarī</s>! <s>Dramiḍī</s>! <s>Drāmiḍī</s>! O burner! O cooker! O crusher! <s>sarale sarale</s>! <s>saralambhe</s>! O tearer of the low, middle, and high! O bearer! <s>mahile mahile</s>! O greatly great! O fetter! O shatterer of fetters! O intoxicated one! O intoxicating one! O tamed one! O wheel! O you with the <s>Cakravāka</s> [birds]! Blaze, blaze! Flame, flame! O flaming one! <s>Śavarī</s>! <s>Śāvarī</s>! O remover of all diseases! <s>cūḍi cūḍi</s>! <s>cūḍini cūḍini</s>! <s>nimi nimi</s>! <s>nimindhari</s>! O mother of the three worlds! O illuminator of the three worlds! O surveyor of the three realms! O bearer of the great <s>Vidyā</s> of the <s>vajra</s>, axe, noose, mace, sword, conch, wheel, trident, and wish-fulfilling gem! Protect, protect me and all beings everywhere, in every place, from all fears of the wicked, from all fears of humans and non-humans, from all diseases! O <s>vajra</s>! O <s>vajra</s>-possessing one! O bearer of <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>! <s>hili hili</s>! <s>mili mili</s>! <s>kili kili</s>! <s>cili cili</s>! <s>sili sili</s>! <s>vara vara</s>! O boon-giver! To the one who has obtained victory everywhere, <s>svāhā</s>! To the tearer of sin, <s>svāhā</s>! To the remover of all diseases, <s>svāhā</s>! To the remover of fear everywhere, <s>svāhā</s>! May there be well-being for me and all beings, <s>svāhā</s>! Peace, <s>svāhā</s>! Prosperity, <s>svāhā</s>! Be victorious, O victorious one! O victorious one! Victory! O stainless one! O vast one, <s>svāhā</s>! To the form of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ</s> <s>bhūri bhūri</s>! O <s>vajra</s>-possessing one! O fulfiller of the heart of the <s>Tathāgata</s>! O sustainer! Strong, strong! O victorious <s>Vidyā</s>, <s>hūṃ hūṃ</s>, <s>phaṭ phaṭ</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text: yasya kasyacin mahābrāhmaṇa anayā tathāgatamūrtyā vidyāmantrapadadhāraṇyā rakṣā kṛtā paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaḥ paripālanaṃ śāntiḥ svastyayanaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavet tasya parikṣīṇam āyuḥ punar eva vivardhate | suciraṃ sukhaṃ ca jīvati | smṛtisaṃpannaś ca bhavati | uccāraṇamātreṇa vā vajrāvamārjanena vākālamaraṇān mahāvyādhibhyaś ca parimucyate | sarvarogāś cāsya praśāmyanti | dairghyaglānyam avamārjanamātreṇa praśamaṃ gacchati | dine dine svādhyāyaṃ kuryān mahāprājño bhavati | tejobalavīryapratibhānasaṃpanno bhavati | sarvapāpakarmāvaraṇāni cāsya niyatavedanīyāni niravaśeṣaṃ parikṣayaṃ yāsyanti | sarvabuddhabodhisattvadevanāgayakṣādīni cāsya ojobalavīryaṃ kāye prakṣepsyanti | mahāprītibahulo bhaviṣyati | antaśo mahābrāhmaṇa iyaṃ mahāvidyāmantrapadarakṣā tiryagyonigatānām api mṛgapakṣiṇāṃ karṇapuṭe nipatiṣyati te sarve 'vaivartikā bhaviṣyanty anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | kaḥ punar vādo ya imāṃ mahāpratisarāṃ dhāraṇīṃ śrāddhaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bhikṣur vā bhikṣuṇī vā upāsako vā upāsikā vā rājā vā rājaputro vā brāhmaṇo vā kṣatriyo vā tadanyo vā yaḥ kaścit sakṛc chroṣyati śrutvā ca mahatyā śraddhayā gauraveṇādhyāśayena likhiṣyati likhāpayiṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati tīvreṇa manasā bhāvayiṣyati parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyati tasya mahābrāhmaṇa aṣṭāv akālamaraṇāni sarvathā na pratikāṅkṣitavyāni | na cāsya kāye mahāvyādhayo bhaviṣyanti | na cāsya śarīre 'gnir na viṣaṃ na śastraṃ na garaṃ na kākhordakiraṇaṃ na mantrakarma na cūrṇayogo na cāṅgaśūlaṃ na jvaro na śiro 'rtir vā | ekāhikadvaitīyakatraitīyakacāturthakasaptāhikā vā jvarāḥ kāye na kramiṣyanti | sa smṛta eva sukhaṃ svapiti | smṛta eva vibudhyate | mahāparinirvāṇalābhī bhaviṣyati | sakṛt sahadharmeṇa mahati mahaiśvaryaṃ cādhigacchati | yatra yatropapadyate tatra tatra jātau jātau jātismaro bhaviṣyati | sarvasattvānāṃ ca priyo bhaviṣyati | vandanīyaś ca bhaviṣyati | sarvanarakatiryagyonigatigahanapretopapattibhyaś ca parimukto bhaviṣyati | yathā cārkamaṇḍalaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ tathā raśmyeva bhāsakaro bhaviṣyati | yathā candramaṇḍalam amṛtena prabhavatāṃ sarvasattvānāṃ kāyaṃ prahlādayati tathā dharmāmṛtena sarvasattvānāṃ cittasaṃtānāni prahlādayiṣyati | sarvaduṣṭayakṣarākṣasabhūtapretapiśācāpasmāraḍākinīgrahavighnavināyakādayaḥ sarve 'sya mahāpratisaravidyārājaprabhāvena na śaktā viheṭhanāṃ kartum | upasaṃkramatāṃ ca teṣām ayaṃ mahāvidyārājā smartavyā | tatas te sarvaduṣṭacittā vidyādharasya vaśyā ājñāśravaṇavidheyā bhavanti | asyā evānubhāvena yad uta mahāpratisarāvidyārājñyā na cāsya śatrubhayaṃ bhaviṣyati | anatikramaṇīyaś ca bhaviṣyati sarvaśatrugaṇai rājarājamahāmātyair brāhmaṇagṛhapatibhiś ca | antaśo 'pi ca vadhyārho vadhakapuruṣair ucchritāny api śastrāṇi khaṇḍakhaṇḍaṃ gacchanti pāṃsumayānīva viśīryante | tasmiṃś ca samaye sarvadharmā asyāmukhībhaviṣyanti | mahac cāsya smṛtibalaṃ bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: O great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, for whomever protection has been made by this <s>Tathāgata</s>-image and <s>vidyā</s>-<s>mantra</s>-<s>dhāraṇī</s>—whoever has received safeguarding, sheltering, guardianship, pacification, and benediction—that one whose lifespan was exhausted shall have it increased again. One lives happily for a long time and becomes endowed with mindfulness. By merely reciting it, or by the <s>vajra</s>-cleansing, one is freed from untimely death and great diseases. All illnesses are pacified. Chronic ailments are calmed by mere cleansing. One who practices daily recitation becomes greatly wise, endowed with energy, strength, vigor, and eloquence. And all obscurations from sinful deeds, even those destined to be certainly experienced, shall be completely exhausted without remainder. All Buddhas, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and others shall infuse vitality, strength, and vigor into that one's body. One shall be filled with great joy. Furthermore, O great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, this great <s>vidyā</s>-<s>mantra</s>-protection, even when it falls upon the ears of animals born in lower realms—birds and beasts—they all shall become irreversible from supreme perfect awakening. What then need be said of a faithful son or daughter of good family, or a monk, nun, layman, laywoman, king, prince, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, or anyone else who hears this <s>Mahāpratisarā dhāraṇī</s> even once and, having heard it, with great faith, reverence, and devoted intention, writes it or has it written, bears it, recites it, meditates upon it with an ardent mind, and explains it extensively to others? For that person, O great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the eight kinds of untimely death are in no way to be expected. No great diseases shall afflict the body. Neither fire, nor poison, nor weapon, nor noxious substance, nor <s>kākhorda</s>-sorcery, nor spell-work, nor powder-application, nor bodily pain, nor fever, nor headache [shall afflict]. Neither one-day, two-day, three-day, four-day, nor seven-day fevers shall enter the body. That one sleeps happily with full awareness and awakens with full awareness. One shall attain the great <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>. With a single [application] along with the <s>Dharma</s>, one attains great sovereignty. Wherever one is reborn, in each and every birth, one shall remember past lives. One shall be beloved of all beings and worthy of veneration. One shall be freed from all unfortunate rebirths in hells, animal wombs, dense [realms of] hungry ghosts, and [other] unfortunate existences. Just as the disk of the sun illuminates all beings with its rays, so shall that one illuminate. Just as the disk of the moon with its nectar-like radiance refreshes the bodies of all beings, so shall that one refresh the mind-streams of all beings with the nectar of <s>Dharma</s>. All hostile <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Bhūtas</s>, <s>Pretas</s>, <s>Piśācas</s>, epilepsy-spirits, <s>Ḍākinīs</s>, planetary afflictions, and <s>Vighnavināyakas</s> (obstacle-makers)—none of them are able to cause harm by the power of this <s>Mahāpratisarā Vidyārāja</s>. And when they approach, this great <s>Vidyārāja</s> should be brought to mind. Then all those of evil intent become subject to the <s>vidyā</s>-bearer, obedient and amenable to commands—by the very power of this <s>Mahāpratisarā Vidyārājñī</s>. No fear of enemies shall befall that one, and that one shall be insurmountable by all hosts of enemies, by kings and great ministers, by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders. Even if one deserves execution, the weapons raised by executioners shatter into pieces and crumble like dust. And at that moment, all <s>dharmas</s> shall become manifest to that one, and great shall be the power of mindfulness.

children.text: rakṣoghnaṃ paramaṃ hy etat pavitraṃ pāpanāśanam |
children.translated_text: This is the supreme destroyer of demons, the most sacred, the annihilator of sins,
the bestower of fortune and wisdom, the increaser of all virtues. (1)
She is the bringer of all auspiciousness, the destroyer of all inauspiciousness,
the shower of good dreams and the destroyer of bad dreams. (2)

children.text: strīpuṃsayoḥ parā rakṣā vidyeyaṃ hi mahābalā |
children.translated_text: For both women and men, this <s>vidyā</s> of great power is the supreme protection;
in forests, wildernesses, and difficult passes, she always liberates instantly. (3)
One obtains all desires, as [promised by] the word of the Perfectly Awakened One;

children.text: patha utpatham āpanna etāṃ vidyām anusmaret || 4 ||
children.translated_text: if one has gone astray from the path, one should recall this <s>vidyā</s>. (4)

children.text: panthānaṃ labhate śīghraṃ bhojanaṃ pānam uttamam |
children.translated_text: One quickly finds the road, and supreme food and drink;

children.text: kāyena manasā vācā yat kṛtaṃ pūrvajanmasu || 5 ||
children.translated_text: whatever was done by body, mind, and speech in former births— (5)

children.text: aśubhaṃ bahuvidhaṃ kiṃcit tat sarvaṃ kṣapayiṣyati |
children.translated_text: all that varied unwholesome [<s>karma</s>] shall be utterly exhausted,

children.text: smaraṇād dhāraṇāc caiva udgrahāl lekhanād api || 6 ||
children.translated_text: by remembering, bearing, taking up, and writing, (6)
by reading, reciting, chanting, and teaching to others;
before long, that one shall attain the course of all <s>dharmas</s>. (7)

children.text: evaṃ hi dharmarase prāpte pāpā gacchanti saṃkṣayam |
children.translated_text: When the essence of <s>Dharma</s> has thus been obtained, sins are utterly destroyed;

children.text: sidhyante sarvakāryāṇi manasā yad yad īpsitam || 8 ||
children.translated_text: all undertakings succeed—whatever is desired by the mind. (8)
In all fears of death, she shall be a refuge for that person;

children.text: rājāgnir udakaṃ caiva vidyud vā taskaro 'pi vā || 9 ||
children.translated_text: [whether from] kings, fire, water, lightning, or thieves, (9)
battles, wars, quarrels, and fierce fanged beasts—

children.text: te sarve pralayaṃ yānti vidyāyā lakṣajāpataḥ || 10 ||
children.translated_text: they all come to destruction by a hundred thousand recitations of this <s>vidyā</s>. (10)
This supreme, accomplished <s>vidyā</s> was taught by all Buddhas;
those who proclaim it do not fail in fulfilling the accumulation of <s>Bodhi</s>. (11)

children.text: sarveṣu caiva sthāneṣu imāṃ vidyāṃ prayojayet |
children.translated_text: In all places one should employ this <s>vidyā</s>,
for whatever undertakings one desires, for the accomplishment of one's own and others' aims. (12)

body.text: sidhyanty ayatnatas tāni vidyāto nātra saṃśayaḥ |
body.translated_text: They are accomplished effortlessly through this <s>vidyā</s>—there is no doubt in this.

children.translated_text: "Now I shall proclaim the healing treatment for the sick.
One should make a square <s>maṇḍala</s> (sacred diagram) with earth and cow dung. (1)
With five-colored powder one should paint the auspicious <s>maṇḍala</s>;

children.text: caturaḥ pūrṇakumbhāṃś ca sthāpayed vidhinā budhaḥ || 2 ||
children.translated_text: the wise one should place four full water-vessels according to the rite. (2)

children.text: puṣpāṇy avakiret tatra dhūpayed dhūpam uttamam |
children.translated_text: One should scatter flowers there and offer the finest incense;
one should perform the <s>bali</s> (offering) ritual—the crusher of the great thousand [evils]. (3)

children.text: pūrvavad gandhapuṣpāṃś ca dadyāc cātra vidhānavit |
children.translated_text: As before, the one who knows the rite should offer fragrant flowers;

children.text: catasras tīrikāḥ sthāpyāḥ sarvāś ca paṭṭabaddhikāḥ || 4 ||
children.translated_text: four curtains should be set up, all bound with cloth. (4)
Having bathed the sick person, then wrapped in clean garments,
with body anointed with auspicious fragrances, one should lead them into the center of the <s>maṇḍala</s>. (5)
Having seated the person facing east, one should recite this <s>vidyā</s>;

children.text: saptaśo japtayā cāsya rakṣāṃ kuryād vicakṣaṇaḥ || 6 ||
children.translated_text: the skilled one should perform the protection by reciting it seven times. (6)
Then, for the sake of the sick person, twenty-one times
one should recite this <s>vidyā</s> for the pacification of all diseases. (7)

children.text: bhūyaś ca sapta vārān vai balikumbhasumantritam |
children.translated_text: And again seven times, having empowered the <s>bali</s>-vessel with <s>mantras</s>,
afterwards the <s>mantra</s>-practitioner should offer the <s>bali</s> and flowers according to the rite. (8)

children.text: ity evaṃ dakṣiṇe pārśve kṣipeta sapta eva tu |
children.translated_text: Thus on the right side one should cast [offerings] seven times,

children.text: paścimāyāṃ ca saptaiva uttarāyāṃ tathā diśi || 9 ||
children.translated_text: on the western side seven times, and on the northern direction likewise. (9)

children.text: adha ūrdhvaṃ tu saptaiva kṛtā rakṣā bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: Below and above also seven times—thus the protection shall be accomplished.
When done thus, O best of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, one is freed from all suffering. (10)
This protection was proclaimed by the <s>Śākyasiṃha</s> (Lion of the Śākyas), the Savior;

children.text: nāsty asyāḥ parā kācid rakṣāvidyā tridhātuke || 11 ||
children.translated_text: there exists no protection-spell in the three realms superior to this. (11)"

children.text: na tasya mṛtyur na jarā na rogo
children.translated_text: "There is no death, no old age, no disease for that one,
nor anything unpleasant, nor separation;
for the one who possesses this well-spoken <s>vidyā</s>—
that one shall be honored by the hosts of death. (1)
<s>Yama</s> himself, the excellent king of <s>Dharma</s>,
shall perform worship with reverence [for that one],
and shall say: 'Go to the city of the gods;
for but a moment would you make this my hell.' (2)
Then, in various kinds of celestial chariots,
the one of great supernatural power goes to the beautiful abode of the gods.
Thus by <s>Kiṃnaras</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>
shall that one be worshipped there always. (3)"

children.text: vajrapāṇiś ca yakṣendra indraś caiva śacīpatiḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, lord of the <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Indra</s>, lord of <s>Śacī</s>,
<s>Hārītī</s> and <s>Pāñcika</s>, and the <s>Lokapālas</s> (World-Guardians) of great power, (1)
the moon and sun with the constellations, and the planets, supremely fierce—

children.text: te ca sarve mahānāgā devatā ṛṣayas tathā || 2 ||
children.translated_text: they all, and the great <s>Nāgas</s>, the deities, and the seers likewise, (2)

children.text: asurā garuḍā gandharvāḥ kiṃnarāś ca mahoragāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Kiṃnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s>—
are constantly attendant for the protection of the one who bears this <s>vidyā</s> of great power. (3)

children.text: likhitāṃ dhārayet prājño bāhau baddhvā maharddhikām |
children.translated_text: The wise one should write it and bear it bound on the arm, this most powerful [spell];

children.text: mahatīṃ labhate pūjāṃ saṃpadaṃ cāpi nityaśaḥ || 4 ||
children.translated_text: one obtains great worship and prosperity constantly. (4)

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān āttamanās te ca bhikṣavas te ca bodhisattvāḥ sā ca sarvāvatī parṣat sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvaś ca loko bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandann iti |
children.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One (<s>Bhagavān</s>). Delighted, those monks (<s>bhikṣus</s>), those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, that entire assembly, and the world with its gods, humans, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s> rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One.

body.text: mahāpratisarāyā mahāvidyārājñyā rakṣāvidhānakalpo vidyādharasyāyaṃ samāptaḥ |
body.translated_text: The ritual prescription for protection (<s>rakṣāvidhānakalpa</s>) of the <s>Mahāpratisarā Mahāvidyārājñī</s>, [belonging to] the spell-bearer (<s>vidyādhara</s>), is hereby concluded.
